docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Alcazaba

Secure, maintained tools for FastAPI Response cache, rate limits, sessions, CSRF, webhooks, a task queue and more, in one package.

Alcazaba (fastapi-alcazaba) gathers the pieces most FastAPI apps end up writing themselves, built with security in mind and tested against real servers. The guide has a page per tool, the examples show them at work in complete apps, and the API reference lists every class and function.

Get started Examples API reference

docs.title: The tools
docs.text:
• Response cache

    @cache for endpoints and functions: one entry for everybody or one per user, invalidation by tag, signed or encrypted entries.

  • Backends

    In memory, Redis, Valkey, GLIDE, memcached or DynamoDB, and a copy in each process in front of them.

  • Pagination

    Pages, limit and offset, and signed cursors, each page cached under its own key.

  • Rate and concurrency limits

    Requests per window and requests at a time, per client or shared, across processes.

  • Idempotency keys

    A retried POST gets the first response instead of running twice.

  • API keys, tokens and codes

    API keys with scopes and expiry, a blocklist of tokens and one-time codes, nothing stored in clear.

  • Sessions, CSRF and security headers

    Sessions you can revoke, requests from other sites refused, the OWASP headers and a body size limit.

  • Audit trail

    Who did what to which resource, and whether it worked: no secrets, signed and chained.

  • Checking uploads

    The real type from the bytes, the size, image dimensions and safe file names.

  • Webhooks and outbound calls

    Standard Webhooks signing and verification, and calls out with a deadline, a breaker and SSRF protection.

  • Errors and observability

    RFC 9457 problem details, request IDs, timeouts, health checks, metrics and traces.

  • Background work

    Scheduled jobs, a task queue, a leader and locks, shared by every process.

  • Operations

    Circuit breakers, maintenance mode and feature flags that every process sees at once.

  • Security model and resilience

    What gets cached and for whom, what the backend is trusted with, and what happens when it fails.

docs.title: Safe by default
docs.text:
The response cache is safe by default:

  • Users never get each other's responses. Requests carrying Authorization or Cookie get their own cache entries and the response is sent as Cache-Control: private, also when the endpoint authenticates through a router dependency.
  • No Redis script injection. FastAPICache.clear(namespace=...) deletes with SCAN + UNLINK: a namespace from user input never reaches a Lua script, and the server isn't blocked by KEYS.
  • Signed or encrypted entries. With a signing_key, every entry carries an HMAC bound to its key: whoever can write to Redis can't plant data, move one user's entry under another user's key, or get a pickle executed. With an encryption_key they're also encrypted (AES-256-GCM): a dump or a backup of Redis doesn't reveal the cached responses.
  • Bounded memory. InMemoryBackend evicts the least recently used entries instead of growing forever with every new query string.
  • Clients can't bypass the cache with Cache-Control: no-cache unless you allow it.
  • Only successful responses are cached, never a 404 or a 500 replayed as a 200.
  • Cache stampede protection: concurrent misses for one key compute once, in each process and, with distributed_lock, across processes.
  • A broken backend doesn't take the app down: every backend call has a timeout, and a circuit breaker stops calling it while it fails.
  • Keys that never repeat are reported: an argument whose repr() changes on every call (a database session, a service) makes every request a miss; Alcazaba warns about it.

And more: early refresh of popular entries, Valkey through valkey-py or Valkey GLIDE, cache hits that return the annotated type (Pydantic models, not dicts), deterministic ETags, the Cache-Status header (Alcazaba; hit; ttl=42, Alcazaba; fwd=miss; stored), the response model in OpenAPI, exclude_params and stale-while-revalidate.

docs.title: License and credits
docs.text:
Apache License 2.0: see LICENSE and NOTICE.

An alcazaba is the walled citadel of an Andalusian city, like those of Almería, Málaga or the Alhambra: walls around what matters, and gates that only let the right things in. The logo is one of its walls, crowned with pointed merlons, whose horseshoe arch opens on a bolt: safe, and fast.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Fuzz targets (fuzz/) for what reads data from outside: the type and size sniffed from uploads and the safe file names, compressed entries, pagination cursors, signed webhooks and audit details, each checking the properties it must keep. ClusterFuzzLite runs them with atheris on pull requests and every week; the unit tests run them on random inputs.

  • fastapi_alcazaba.core.canonical_json: the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (RFC 8785), the one serialization of a JSON value that every language implementing it writes the same.

  • Paginated responses link to the pages around them in the Link header (RFC 8288): first, prev, next and last by page number or by limit and offset, first and next by cursor. The links keep the request's other query parameters and are relative to the host. Pages served by @cache get them too, made for the request they answer and never stored with the entry. The page parameters carry them as links (a PageLinks), left out of their repr and so of cache keys.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• A folder per tool, each exporting its public names (from fastapi_alcazaba.pagination import Page); the main class of each tool is still importable from fastapi_alcazaba. The modules moved, with nothing left at their old paths:

    • response_cache: decorator (cache), caches (was cache: Cache, FastAPICache, get_cache), coder, key_builder (and KeyBuilder, from types), compression;
    • backends: Backend, from types;
    • rate_limit: limiter, concurrency;
    • auth: apikeys, tokens;
    • security: sessions, csrf, and middleware's SecurityHeadersMiddleware and BodySizeLimitMiddleware;
    • observability: problems, request_id, timeouts, health;
    • background: scheduler, tasks, leader, locks;
    • operations: breaker, flags, maintenance;
    • outbound: the transports of outbound;
    • core: errors, integrity, encryption, canonical, resilience;
    • telemetry: metrics, tracing;
    • pagination, idempotency, audit, uploads and webhooks keep their names, now folders.

    Loggers are named after the modules where they are (fastapi_alcazaba.observability.timeouts); metrics, spans and the fastapi_alcazaba.audit.events logger keep their names. - Cached responses report the result in the Cache-Status header of RFC 9211 instead of X-FastAPI-Cache: Alcazaba; hit; ttl=42 with the seconds the entry has left, or why the request reached the endpoint (fwd=miss, stale for an early refresh, request for a client's no-cache, method, bypass with the cache off), stored when its response was kept and collapsed when it waited for another request's. Responses that weren't cached get the header too. FastAPICache.init(cache_status_header=...) is now cache_status=, the cache's name (None leaves the header out), and get_cache_status_header() is get_cache_status(). - The audit trail's signatures cover the event's RFC 8785 canonical JSON, after the context fastapi_alcazaba/audit2 and a NUL byte, so that any language can check them; events signed by 0.2.0 no longer verify. Details keep to I-JSON for it: integers beyond 2⁵³ are recorded as text, and lone surrogates in any text of an event as U+FFFD. - The API reference has a page per tool (cache, backends, limits, audit...) with an index of them, instead of one long page; each object is set apart, with its kind and its signature. - So does the guide: a Guide tab starts with getting started and has a page per tool, and the documentation's home page introduces the tools instead of holding the whole README. - The documentation has a site per version, with a selector in the header: dev for what's on main and X.Y for each release from 0.3, the newest being latest, where the site's address leads. The other versions say they're not the latest.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• FastAPIPaginationCursor.decode() raised a TypeError, instead of the 400 of an invalid cursor, for a signed cursor with non-ASCII characters (the route's own parameter never lets one in).
  • verify_audit_trail() raised a TypeError for an event whose signature had non-ASCII characters, instead of reporting it as altered.
  • safe_filename() with a max_length under 64 bytes could give a longer name when the extension was short in characters but long in bytes (emoji): such an extension is now dropped.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Rate limiting: FastAPIRateLimiter (fastapi_alcazaba.limiter), a FastAPI dependency that lets each client make times requests per sliding window to a route, with a 429 and Retry-After beyond. The counters live in the cache's backend, shared by every process, behind its timeout and circuit breaker (fail_open). A port of fastapi-limiter without its weaknesses: clients are told apart by the address the ASGI server reports, not by X-Forwarded-For (which any client can set), and IPv6 addresses by their /64 network (client_network for other sizes); the budget is per route, not per URL (/items/1, /items/2… had one each); requests over the limit don't count, checked and counted atomically. name shares a budget across routes, cost makes a route take more of it, identifier counts per user, and hit() limits anything else (WebSocket messages, login attempts). Responses carry the RateLimit and RateLimit-Policy headers of the IETF draft. Each process refuses a client with nothing left without asking the backend until something fits again.
  • Counters in every backend, for the rate limiter: Backend.incr, Backend.get_counter, Backend.incr_window (a Lua script on Redis, Valkey and GLIDE, a conditional write on DynamoDB) and Backend.supports_counters.
  • The fastapi_alcazaba.rate_limit metric.
  • get_cache works in WebSocket routes.
  • Pagination without another library (fastapi_alcazaba.pagination): FastAPIPagination (page and size), FastAPIPaginationLimitOffset and FastAPIPaginationCursor, each configured once with its limits and used as a dependency that checks the query parameters, and with a paginate for a whole list or a page already queried. Page and LimitOffsetPage have the JSON of fastapi-pagination's. Cursors are keyset pagination on a unique sort key that keeps its types (datetimes, UUIDs, decimals…), optionally signed (HMAC-SHA256, rotation), with a 400 for invalid ones. The page parameters are arguments of the endpoint, so @cache keeps each page under its own key. An example (examples/pagination): a catalogue cached page by page, whole, or by cursor.
  • Locks shared by every process: Cache.lock() / FastAPICache.lock() (fastapi_alcazaba.locks), with an expiry, renewal while held, a random token per holder, waiting (wait) and LockNotAcquired. InMemoryBackend (within the process) and DynamoBackend (conditional writes) can now hold locks, and backends gain extend_lock.
  • Idempotency keys: IdempotencyMiddleware and require_idempotency_key (fastapi_alcazaba.idempotency, draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header). A retried POST or PATCH gets the first response (Idempotent-Replayed: true) and runs once; a retry while it runs gets a 409, the same key for another request a 422. Keys are per client (Authorization by default), responses are stored signed or encrypted, and a failing backend answers 503 unless fail_open=True.
  • Revoked tokens and one-time codes (fastapi_alcazaba.tokens): TokenBlocklist keeps revoked JWTs (revoke, by jti) and subjects logged out everywhere (revoke_subject) in the cache's backend until the tokens would have expired, and refuses them when the backend fails unless fail_open=True. OneTimeCodes issues e-mail or SMS codes, stored as HMACs with a secret, with an expiry, a limit of guesses and single use that holds under concurrent requests.
  • Outbound calls: ResilientTransport (fastapi_alcazaba.outbound), an httpx2/httpx transport that gives each call a deadline for the whole response (httpx's timeouts are per phase, so a server that trickles bytes kept a request open forever) and a circuit breaker per origin (CircuitOpenError, an httpx.TransportError). 5xx responses count as failures (failure_statuses), the caller's own errors (an illegal header, an unsupported scheme) don't. max_response_size caps the bytes read (ResponseTooLargeError).
  • SecurityHeadersMiddleware and BodySizeLimitMiddleware (fastapi_alcazaba.middleware): the OWASP REST security headers on every response (HSTS only over HTTPS, a strict CSP for everything but HTML), and a 413 for request bodies over a size limit, checked from Content-Length and counted for chunked bodies.
  • Health checks: health_router() (fastapi_alcazaba.health) adds /health/live (the process answers) and /health/ready (the app's checks run concurrently with timeouts: 200 ok or degraded, 503 fail), with a non-critical check of the cache's backend. Errors are logged, never returned, and concurrent probes share one run, reused for reuse_for seconds.
  • Scheduled jobs: FastAPIScheduler (fastapi_alcazaba.scheduler) runs async or sync jobs every N seconds (every) or by a cron expression in a time zone (cron, with its own parser: ranges, steps, names, @daily…; clock changes handled as cronie does), in every process and each tick once across them: ticks are claimed with an atomic counter in the backend, and a lock held while a job runs keeps long runs from overlapping elsewhere (exclusive=False runs a job everywhere). Errors are logged and counted without stopping the schedule, a failing backend skips the tick unless fail_open=True, and lifespan / async with start and stop it with a grace period for running jobs.
  • Circuit breakers: FastAPIBreaker (fastapi_alcazaba.breaker) for any dependency, as a decorator of async or sync functions or around a block (attempt()), with a timeout for async calls, failures and exclude to say what counts, and BreakerOpen, an HTTPException that FastAPI answers with a 503 and Retry-After.
  • Problem details (fastapi_alcazaba.problems): FastAPIProblemDetails().install(app) answers HTTPExceptions, validation errors and unhandled exceptions with RFC 9457 application/problem+json (type, title, status, detail, instance and the request_id of RequestIDMiddleware), keeping the exceptions' headers (Retry-After, WWW-Authenticate…). 5xx details are never sent (a hidden HTTPException detail is logged); 4xx ones are unless expose_detail=False; validation errors list loc, msg and type, never FastAPI's input (which echoes passwords) nor ctx, at most max_errors. Unhandled exceptions get a bare 500 and are still raised again for the server to log. Problem is an HTTPException with a type URI, a title and checked extension members; problems.response() answers one from your own exception handlers.
  • Request IDs (fastapi_alcazaba.request_id): RequestIDMiddleware, a pure ASGI middleware that gives every HTTP request and WebSocket an ID, reusing the incoming X-Request-ID only when it's a single value safe to log ([A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}, trust_incoming=False to never reuse it) and making a random 128-bit one otherwise, and sends it back in the response. request_id() returns it while the request is handled (sync endpoints' threads included), and it stays set after an unhandled exception so that the 500 handler and the server's error log still know the request. RequestIDLogFilter puts it in log records as %(request_id)s.
  • Request timeouts (fastapi_alcazaba.timeouts): RequestTimeoutMiddleware, a pure ASGI middleware that gives every HTTP request a deadline (timeout=30 seconds, other ones by path prefix with paths, None for none) from its arrival until its response has been sent, reading the body included. At the deadline the app is cancelled (its finally blocks and yield dependencies' exits run) and the client gets a 504; a response already streaming is cut by raising the TimeoutError again, so that the server closes the connection instead of ending a short body as if it were complete. Background tasks after the response have no deadline; WebSockets and lifespan events go through untouched.
  • Concurrency limits: FastAPIConcurrencyLimiter (fastapi_alcazaba.concurrency), a FastAPI dependency (with yield) that lets at most limit requests run at the same time across every process, per route, per name shared by routes, or per client (identifier, answered with a 429 instead of a 503), with Retry-After. The semaphore is limit (up to 100) renewed locks in the cache's backend, tried in random order and expiring if their holder dies; requests wait up to wait seconds with jittered backoff. The slot is held until the response has been sent (the whole body of a StreamingResponse since FastAPI 0.118; scope="function" releases it earlier), and while a WebSocket is open. slot() takes one outside requests. When the backend fails, each process enforces the limit on its own (fail_open=False refuses with a 503).
  • Leader election: FastAPILeader (fastapi_alcazaba.leader) elects one process among those sharing the cache's backend, on a renewed lock, and runs the async functions given to run (a decorator) while it leads: they're cancelled when the leadership is lost or the leader stops, and the process campaigns again. start()/stop(), lifespan and async with; is_leader works from sync code too. A stopping leader releases the lock for a quick hand-over; a dead one is replaced within ttl and a third. Nobody is elected while the backend fails.
  • Maintenance mode: FastAPIMaintenance (fastapi_alcazaba.maintenance) with enable(message, retry_after), disable() and status(), shared by every process through the cache's backend, and MaintenanceMiddleware, a pure ASGI middleware that answers 503 with Retry-After (and closes WebSockets with 1013) while it's on, except for allow_paths and the requests allow lets through. Each process keeps a copy of the state refreshed at most every refresh seconds, so requests don't reach the backend; when the backend fails, the last state read stays. The state is sealed with the cache's signing or encryption key when it has one.
  • Feature flags: FastAPIFeatureFlags (fastapi_alcazaba.flags) stores flags in the cache's backend: set(name, enabled=..., percentage=..., allow=..., deny=...), delete, get, enabled(name, subject, default) and require(name, subject=...), a FastAPI dependency that answers 404 while the flag is off, without revealing it. Percentage rollouts are sticky (a hash of the flag and the subject) and only grow with the percentage. Without a percentage a flag is for everybody, or only for its allow list when it has one. Each process keeps definitions for refresh seconds and falls back on the last one read, or the default, when the backend fails. Subjects are stored as salted SHA-256 digests, never in clear, and definitions are sealed with the cache's signing or encryption key when it has one.
  • API keys (fastapi_alcazaba.apikeys): FastAPIAPIKeys(lookup), a dependency that authenticates machine clients by keys like ak_<id>_<secret> (80-bit id, 256-bit secret), read from X-API-Key or, with bearer=True, Authorization: Bearer, both declared in the OpenAPI schema. generate() returns the key, to show once, and an APIKeyRecord to store: a SHA-256 digest of the secret bound to its id, an HMAC with an optional pepper (rotation), scopes and an expiry. The app's own lookup(key_id) (async or sync, in a thread) returns its row, which the dependency returns after a constant-time comparison and the expiry check; every failure gets the same 401 with WWW-Authenticate, and require(*scopes) a 403. Keys are never logged. An optional per-process cache of records (cache_ttl, cache_size, forget()) trades revocation latency for fewer lookups.
  • Signed webhooks (fastapi_alcazaba.webhooks), compatible with Standard Webhooks (Svix, Supabase, Clerk, Resend...): WebhookSigner signs outgoing ones (whsec_ secrets, a random webhook-id, every secret of a rotation), and FastAPIWebhooks, a dependency, verifies incoming ones over the raw body, which the endpoint can still read (capped by max_body_size, 413 beyond), with a timestamp tolerance both ways, constant-time comparison against every secret, and replay protection: each accepted delivery is counted in the cache's backend (hashed, under state_key) until it can't be accepted anymore, while the sender's retries (new timestamp and signature) still go through. Wrong signatures, stale timestamps and replays get the same 401; a failing backend a 503 (fail_open to accept instead). verify() checks a message without the replay check.
  • SSRF protection for outbound calls: SSRFGuardTransport (fastapi_alcazaba.outbound), an httpx transport that resolves the host itself and refuses the request (BlockedDestinationError, an httpx.RequestError that ResilientTransport doesn't count against the origin) when any of its addresses isn't public: private, loopback, link-local and cloud metadata, carrier-grade NAT, multicast, reserved and documentation ranges, unique-local IPv6, and IPv4-mapped, NAT64, 6to4 and Teredo forms. Literal addresses and numeric spellings are caught too. The connection is pinned to the checked address (URL rewritten to it, Host kept, SNI and certificate checked against the name), so DNS rebinding can't swap it; every redirect hop is checked; one address of the other family is tried if the first can't connect. allow lets internal names (*. for subdomains) and networks through, ports restricts ports, each host name gets its own connection pool (max_hosts), and proxied inner transports are refused. Composes as ResilientTransport(SSRFGuardTransport()).
  • CSRF protection: CSRFMiddleware (fastapi_alcazaba.csrf), a plain ASGI middleware that refuses with a 403 the unsafe requests a page on another site made the browser send with the user's cookies or HTTP authentication. It trusts Sec-Fetch-Site (same-origin passes, same-site and cross-site only from trusted_origins), and else requires an Origin or Referer of the app's own origin (scheme and Host as the server sees them) or a trusted one; Origin: null and requests with neither are refused. Requests without cookies go through (token APIs aren't exposed), except form submissions from other sites (login CSRF); check_all checks everything. exempt_paths skips prefixes. require_token adds a double-submit token (a __Host- cookie compared in constant time with a header, also in request.state.csrf_token). WebSocket handshakes are checked too, against cross-site WebSocket hijacking.
  • Server-side sessions: ServerSessionMiddleware (fastapi_alcazaba.sessions), a plain ASGI middleware that keeps each browser's session in the cache's backend and only a random 256-bit id in the cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax), so that, unlike Starlette's signed-cookie sessions, the client can't read it and logging out revokes it. request.session works as usual. The data is stored under a digest of the id, sealed with the cache's signing or encryption key, saved only when it changed (nested changes too), JSON-only with a size limit, and expires after max_age and idle_timeout. Ids are always generated by the server; rotate_session (at login, against session fixation) and clear_session (at logout) are included. A backend that can't be read gives an empty session; a change that can't be saved gives a 503.
  • Upload checks with nothing but the standard library (fastapi_alcazaba.uploads): FastAPIUploads(types, max_size=..., max_pixels=...), a dependency (or check(file)) that reads the upload in chunks, counting its size whatever UploadFile.size says (413), detects its real type from its bytes (415 when it isn't allowed), refuses images with more than max_pixels pixels (decompression bombs, 413) and returns a CheckedFile read back to its start, with the detected type, size, dimensions, extension and a safe name. sniff(data) tells PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, PDF, ZIP, GZIP, MP4, QuickTime, UTF-8 text, and Office documents (from the content types the archive declares, macro-enabled ones apart) from each other, and keeps HTML, SVG and XML apart from text; SVG is never an image. image_size(data) reads image dimensions from their headers, and safe_filename(name) makes a client's file name safe to display and to use on any file system.
  • Task queue: FastAPITaskQueue (fastapi_alcazaba.tasks), on Redis 6.2+ or Valkey streams (clusters too). @queue.task() registers async or sync functions; await queue.enqueue(task, *args, delay=...) queues a run with JSON arguments checked against the function; the processes that start() it (or use lifespan) run them, concurrency at a time. Delivery is at least once: tasks are acknowledged when they finish, those of a worker that stopped answering are taken over after visibility_timeout (heartbeats keep long ones), and one handed out more than max_deliveries times is dead-lettered. Failures are retried with exponential backoff and jitter, then dead-lettered with the type of their error only (dead_letters(), requeue_dead_letters(), discard_dead_letters()). Only registered tasks run, never pickle; with the cache's signing or encryption key every task is sealed and bound to its queue, so planted or altered ones are refused and dead-lettered, never run. Delayed tasks move to the stream atomically, the queue is bounded (QueueFull) and payloads are size-capped. stop() gives running tasks grace seconds and puts back those it cancels.
  • Telemetry for the tools: each run of a scheduled job, and of a task (linked to the span that enqueued it), is the root span of a trace of its own; rate-limit, breaker, outbound-breaker and CSRF refusals and breaker transitions are events on the request's span, and idempotency outcomes an attribute of it. New metrics: fastapi_alcazaba.breaker.calls, .breaker.transitions, .scheduler.runs, .idempotency, .tokens.checks, .otp.verifications, .lock.wait, .lock.lost, .health.checks, .health.check.duration, .concurrency, .leader.transitions, .maintenance.refused, .flags.evaluations, .problems, .request_timeouts, .request_ids, .outbound.breaker, .outbound.ssrf.blocked, .webhooks, .api_keys, .csrf.refused, .sessions, .uploads, .uploads.size, .tasks.enqueued, .tasks, .tasks.duration and .tasks.reclaimed. The README shows the recommended setup (OpenTelemetry's zero-code instrumentation and its standard variables): Alcazaba only uses the API.
  • Locks, rate-limit counters, revoked tokens, one-time codes and idempotency records live under {prefix}! (Cache.state_key), apart from the cached responses: clear() never frees a held lock, resets a limit or takes a revocation back, and InMemoryBackend gives them a store of their own that caching responses never evicts.
  • Backend.invalidate_tags_with_keys: an invalidation that also tells which keys it deleted.
  • Examples for the tools (examples/): small, complete apps for the response cache, pagination, rate and concurrency limits, idempotency keys, API keys and one-time codes, a browser app with sessions and CSRF protection, uploads, webhooks, errors and observability, background work and operations. Each is tested with the library and has a page in the documentation's new Examples section, with how to run it and what it answers.
  • A logo and a social card, and the documentation's theme in the project's colours.
  • RedisBackend.client and ValkeyBackend.client: the client the backend talks through.
  • pylint, configured in pyproject.toml, runs with ruff and mypy in make lint, pre-commit and CI.
  • FastAPIBreaker.reset() closes a breaker by hand (the dependency is back, or between tests); failure_threshold and reset_timeout can be read back.
  • forget() on FastAPIMaintenance, FastAPIFeatureFlags and FastAPIRateLimiter drops what each process keeps (its copies of the state, the clients it refuses without asking the backend). A new cache drops it by itself, as each test's lifespan sets one up.
  • SSRFGuardTransport.check(url): checks a URL as a request to it would be, without sending anything, to refuse a webhook's endpoint when it's registered.
  • With FastAPIProblemDetails installed, Alcazaba's middlewares answer with problems too (the 504 of a timeout, the 413 of a body too large, the 503 of maintenance, the 403 of CSRF...), and the error responses keep the rate limiters' RateLimit headers.
  • scripts/check_signatures.py, in make lint, make format, pre-commit and CI: a signature that doesn't fit on one line has one parameter per line, the last one with a comma.
  • An audit trail (FastAPIAudit, fastapi_alcazaba.audit): who did what to which resource, whether it worked, and the request it came from. audit.action() is a dependency that writes the event when the endpoint ends (success, denied for a 401 or a 403, failure with the exception's type and status, never its message), the refusals of the authentication included; audit.log() and audit.record() work outside endpoints. Events carry the request ID, the trace, the route template (never the path) and the client's address; their details keep no secrets (values under keys such as password or token, and credentials, are redacted) and are bounded. They go to the fastapi_alcazaba.audit.events logger as JSON lines, which warns when it outputs nothing, or to sinks of your own. With a signing_key they're signed and chained, and verify_audit_trail() finds the ones altered, forged or removed. A sink that fails is logged with the event and counted, and an event is written even if its request is cancelled. The fastapi_alcazaba.audit and fastapi_alcazaba.audit.undelivered metrics, and an example.
  • Every parameter that takes a key or a secret (signing_key, encryption_key, pepper, the secrets of one-time codes, cursors and webhooks...) also takes pydantic's SecretStr or SecretBytes, as pydantic-settings loads them, so the value stays out of the settings' repr until it's used. The examples read their configuration with pydantic-settings, from the environment or a .env file.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• CircuitBreaker.allow() returns the state the call goes through in ("closed", or "half-open" for the single trial) or None when it's refused, instead of a bool; truthiness is the same.
  • Development, CI and releases use Python's own venv and pip (26.2 or later) instead of uv. make deps sets up .venv; the dependency groups of pyproject.toml install with pip's --group; pip's --uploaded-prior-to P3D keeps releases younger than three days out; the SBOM comes from pip's installation report, with the hashes of the files. There's no lock file: CI installs the latest releases that are at least three days old.
  • A backend asked for something it can't do (locks, tags, counters) raises a NotImplementedError that says so, e.g. MemcachedBackend can't hold locks, instead of one without a message.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• TieredBackend: a tag invalidation didn't reach the copies of processes that had only read the entry (they never saw its tags), not even in the process that invalidated, so they kept serving it for up to local_ttl. Invalidations now name the keys they deleted.
  • TieredBackend: a value read from the shared backend, or written to it, while an invalidation arrived could be kept as the local copy although it was already the old one.
  • The circuit breaker let a second trial through while the first one ran, when a call that wasn't the trial was cancelled.
  • TieredBackend with a client that has a socket_timeout: the subscription to the invalidation channel ended every time the channel was quiet for that long, emptying the local level and logging a warning each time. The channel is now read with its own timeout and pinged when quiet; a connection that died silently is given up within 10 seconds, and a reconnection made by the client itself empties the local level (messages may have been missed).
  • DynamoBackend.clear(key=...): of several deletes of one entry at the same time, more than one could be told that it was there. The delete is now conditional, so exactly one is, and a one-time code works only once on DynamoDB too.
  • Lock.release() (and leaving async with cache.lock(...)) could wait forever when the client swallowed the cancellation of a renewal under way (fakeredis does on Python 3.11): the renewals now stop as soon as the lock is released.
First release of Alcazaba.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Per-user cache entries for requests with Authorization or Cookie (vary_headers), sent as Cache-Control: private with Vary: one user's response is never served to another.
  • RedisBackend.clear(namespace=...) no longer builds a Lua script from the namespace (command injection) nor runs KEYS (blocks the server): SCAN + UNLINK, with glob characters escaped.
  • Optional HMAC-SHA256 signing of entries, bound to their key (signing_key, with rotation). PickleCoder without it raises an UnsignedEntriesWarning.
  • InMemoryBackend is bounded (max_size, LRU) and no longer shared between instances.
  • Clients can no longer bypass the cache with Cache-Control unless respect_cache_control=True.
  • Only 200 responses without no-store are cached.
  • JSON type markers can no longer be triggered by user data.
  • SHA-256 instead of MD5 for keys and ETags.
  • Cache stampede protection (single_flight).
  • The Redis example no longer serves its working directory as static files.
  • UnstableCacheKeyWarning when the default key includes an argument whose repr() changes on every call (a database session, an injected service), which made every request a miss.
  • Backend calls have a timeout (backend_timeout) and go through a circuit breaker (circuit_breaker_failures, circuit_breaker_reset): a hanging backend no longer slows every request down.
  • max_value_size keeps oversized values out of the backend.
  • Optional encryption of the entries (encryption_key, crypto extra): AES-256-GCM with a per-entry key derived by HKDF and the cache key as associated data, with key rotation.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• ValkeyBackend (valkey-py) and GlideBackend (Valkey GLIDE), standalone and cluster.
  • Invalidation by tag: @cache(tags=...) and FastAPICache.invalidate_tags() (in-memory, Redis, Valkey, GLIDE).
  • distributed_lock: one process computes a missing value while the others wait for it.
  • early_refresh: probabilistic refresh of entries near their expiry; a failed refresh serves the cached value.
  • OpenTelemetry metrics (otel extra): lookups, stores, entry sizes, backend durations and errors; and traces: a span per cached call with its result, and one per backend call.
  • Cache instances (one per app, or several with different settings) with their own cached() decorator, get_or_set() for caching inside endpoints, invalidate_tags(), clear() and close(), and the get_cache FastAPI dependency. FastAPICache is now a global Cache.
  • TieredBackend: a per-process memory level in front of any backend, kept in step across processes by pub/sub invalidations (Redis, Valkey) or bounded by local_ttl.
  • GlideBackend reads TTL and value in one round trip (a batch) instead of two.
  • Compression of large entries (compression="zstd" or "zlib"), read back whatever the setting and bounded against decompression bombs.
  • JsonCoder encodes through pydantic-core and validates hits straight from the bytes: 8 times faster encoding of models, 1.4 times faster hits.
  • exclude_params; stale_while_revalidate; MemcachedBackend and DynamoBackend can delete single keys; DynamoBackend(endpoint_url=...); cache_status_header="" turns the header off.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Cache hits return the annotated return type (Pydantic models, dataclasses).
  • Deterministic, quoted ETags; If-None-Match lists, weak tags and *.
  • The response model appears in OpenAPI.
  • No Cache-Control: max-age=None; headers also reach Responses returned by the endpoint.
  • FastAPICache.clear(key=...) with a prefix no longer clears the whole prefix.
  • Entries that can't be decoded are recomputed instead of failing.
  • Importing works without jinja2 (Starlette 1.x).
  • In-memory entries without expire no longer expire immediately; memcached expirations over 30 days; the settings of one call no longer leak into the next.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Distribution fastapi-alcazaba, import package fastapi_alcazaba. Python 3.11+ (3.10 reached its end of life in October 2026), Pydantic v2.
  • redis is optional; uvicorn and pendulum are no longer dependencies.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
make deps                     # .venv (Python's venv and pip), with every extra and the dev tools
.venv/bin/pytest              # unit tests
make services-up              # Redis, Valkey, a Valkey cluster, memcached and DynamoDB Local
make test-integration         # every backend against those servers
make services-down
make mutation                 # mutation testing (slow; CI runs it weekly)
make lint                     # ruff, ruff format --check, mypy --strict, pylint
make docs                     # the documentation, built as CI does (make docs-serve to preview it)

Tests run in a random order (pytest-randomly; the seed is printed to reproduce a failure), and CI fails a pull request with a benchmark more than 50 % slower than main's, compared with the others so the speed of the runner doesn't count. See CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Deployment and releases
docs.text: Alcazaba is released from GitHub Actions: a vX.Y.Z tag builds the distributions, generates the SBOM, signs everything with Sigstore (no keys to keep), publishes to TestPyPI, checks that version installs, and publishes to PyPI after a manual approval. The repository is nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba.

docs.title: 1. Repository
docs.text:
git remote add origin git@github.com:nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba.git
git push -u origin main

The project URLs in pyproject.toml already point to it.

docs.title: 2. Repository settings
docs.text:
• Actions → General → Workflow permissions: read repository contents (the workflows ask for more per job).
  • Rules → Rulesets:
    • main: block force pushes and deletion, require a linear history. With a single maintainer pushing to it; with more, require a pull request and the status checks of CI (Lint and type check, Unit and integration tests (3.11) … (3.14), End-to-end, Package, Audit dependencies, Docs) too.
    • Tags v*: block updates and deletion (a published version must never move), and only the repository's admins create them (a second ruleset, so that their bypass is for creating only).
  • Environments:
    • testpypi: deployment tags v*.
    • pypi: deployment tags v*, required reviewer: you (the approval before PyPI).
    • github-pages: created when Pages is enabled; deployment branch main, from which the Docs workflow deploys every version.
  • Pages: source "GitHub Actions". The Docs workflow keeps a site per version in the gh-pages branch, which its first run creates: dev for main, X.Y for each release.
  • Security: Dependabot alerts and security updates, secret scanning with push protection, private vulnerability reporting (SECURITY.md points there), code scanning (CodeQL and Scorecard upload their results).

docs.title: 3. Trusted publishers
docs.text:
Before the first release the project doesn't exist on the indexes: add a pending publisher on TestPyPI and on PyPI:

Field TestPyPI PyPI PyPI project name fastapi-alcazaba fastapi-alcazaba Owner nonodev96 nonodev96 Repository fastapi-alcazaba fastapi-alcazaba Workflow release.yml release.yml Environment testpypi pypi

No API token is created or stored anywhere: the workflow proves its identity with OIDC.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
1. Move the Unreleased notes of CHANGELOG.md under ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD and merge to main; wait for CI.

  2. Tag the merge commit on main and push the tag:

    git switch main && git pull
git tag vX.Y.Z
git push origin vX.Y.Z

  3. The Release workflow:

    1. checks that the tag is a version on main and runs every suite;
    2. builds the sdist and the wheel (the version comes from the tag, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit);
    3. generates the CycloneDX SBOM and validates it;
    4. signs: GitHub attestations of build provenance (SLSA) and of the SBOM, plus a Sigstore bundle per file;
    5. publishes to TestPyPI and installs that version in a clean environment (smoke test);
    6. waits for your approval in the pypi environment, then publishes to PyPI with PEP 740 attestations;
    7. creates the GitHub release with the distributions, the SBOM, the provenance, the Sigstore bundles and the notes of that version from the changelog;
    8. runs the Docs workflow, which publishes the documentation of the release as X.Y, with the latest alias that the root of the site leads to.

Pre-releases (vX.Y.ZrcN, aN, bN) stop after TestPyPI and become GitHub pre-releases, with no documentation of their own. They take the changelog section of the version they lead to (v0.1.0rc1 → ## [0.1.0]), which can still say Unreleased: a first rc tries the whole pipeline without spending the version.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
• Nothing reaches PyPI until you approve it: reject the deployment and fix.
  • A version can't be uploaded twice. Published something broken? Yank it on PyPI (it stays installable only when pinned exactly) and release X.Y.Z+1.
  • Don't move or reuse a tag that was released.

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text: Only the latest release of fastapi-alcazaba gets security fixes.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text:
Please don't open a public issue. Report it privately through GitHub's security advisories for this repository, with:

  • the affected version and backend,
  • how to reproduce it (a minimal app is ideal),
  • the impact you expect.

You'll get an answer within a week. Once a fix is released, the advisory is published with credit to you, unless you prefer otherwise.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
In scope: anything that lets a request read another user's cached data, write or poison entries, run code, or exhaust the server through the cache; and anything that lets a client get past a rate limiter, or use up someone else's budget, other than by having several IPv4 addresses, IPv6 /64 networks or identities. The same goes for the other tools: getting another client's response through an idempotency key or a request run twice, a lock held by two processes while their renewals work, a revoked token accepted or a one-time code guessed beyond its attempts, a header injected or a body over the limit accepted by the middlewares, errors leaked by the health checks, an exclusive scheduled job run twice for one tick while the backend works, and a call let through an open circuit breaker.

Out of scope: problems that need write access to the backend when no signing_key or encryption_key is configured, reading the backend when no encryption_key is configured (the README explains when each key is needed), and denial of service of the backend itself.

docs.title: Supply chain
docs.text: Releases are built and published from GitHub Actions with PyPI trusted publishing (no API tokens) and carry PyPI attestations. The workflows pin every action to a commit and are checked with zizmor.

docs.title: Verifying a release
docs.text:
Every release is signed with Sigstore by the GitHub Actions workflow that built it: there's no key to trust, only the identity of the workflow (nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba, .github/workflows/release.yml, the tag). Replace X.Y.Z below with the version. The tools, in a virtual environment of their own:

python3 -m venv verify && verify/bin/pip install pypi-attestations sigstore

docs.title: What PyPI serves
docs.text:
PyPI keeps the PEP 740 attestations published with each file:

verify/bin/pypi-attestations verify pypi \
  --repository https://github.com/nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba \
  pypi:fastapi_alcazaba-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl

docs.title: GitHub attestations
docs.text:
Build provenance (SLSA v1) and SBOM attestations, for any copy of the files:

gh attestation verify fastapi_alcazaba-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl --repo nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba
gh attestation verify fastapi_alcazaba-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl --repo nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba \
  --predicate-type https://cyclonedx.org/bom

The release carries the provenance too, fastapi-alcazaba-X.Y.Z.intoto.jsonl (the Sigstore bundle of the attestation, one JSON line): with it, gh attestation verify doesn't ask GitHub for it, and checks the repository's name as the certificate recorded it when the release was built.

gh attestation verify fastapi_alcazaba-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl --repo nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba \
  --bundle fastapi-alcazaba-X.Y.Z.intoto.jsonl

docs.title: Sigstore bundles of the GitHub release
docs.text:
Each file of the release but the provenance has a .sigstore.json bundle next to it:

verify/bin/sigstore verify github fastapi_alcazaba-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl \
  --bundle fastapi_alcazaba-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl.sigstore.json \
  --repository nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba --ref refs/tags/vX.Y.Z --trigger push

docs.title: The SBOM
docs.text:
fastapi-alcazaba-X.Y.Z.cdx.json (CycloneDX 1.5) lists every runtime dependency, with every extra, at the versions installing it resolved to when it was released, with their licences and the hashes of their files. Scan it for known vulnerabilities:

osv-scanner scan --sbom fastapi-alcazaba-X.Y.Z.cdx.json

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Each example is a small, complete FastAPI app in the repository's examples/ folder, written the way the tools are meant to be used in production, and tested with the library on every change. They keep their state in memory so that they run without any server; in production, Redis or Valkey lets every process share it. Only the background work needs one.

  • Response cache

    Shared entries for public pages, private ones per user, invalidation by tag and get_or_set.

  • Pagination

    Pages, a whole list sliced into pages and signed cursors, each cached its own way.

  • Rate and concurrency limits

    Requests per client and per user, shared budgets, and at most N expensive calls at a time.

  • Idempotency keys

    A retried payment gets the first response instead of charging twice.

  • API keys, tokens and codes

    Keys stored as digests with scopes, one-time login codes and revoked tokens.

  • A browser app

    Server-side sessions, CSRF protection and security headers for a cookie-based app.

  • Audit trail

    Who changed or deleted which account, refusals included, signed and chained.

  • Checking uploads

    The real type of a file from its bytes, size and pixel limits, and safe names.

  • Webhooks in and out

    Signed webhooks received without replays, and sent to user URLs without SSRF.

  • Errors and observability

    Problem details, request IDs in logs and responses, deadlines and health checks.

  • Background work

    Scheduled jobs, a leader among processes and a task queue on Redis streams.

  • Operations

    Maintenance mode, feature flags and circuit breakers, switched at runtime.

docs.title: Running them
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository, each one starts with uvicorn:

git clone https://github.com/nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba.git
cd fastapi-alcazaba
make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.cache.main:app

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs to try its endpoints from the browser. The keys and secrets they need come from environment variables, with a throwaway value for trying them out: set real ones in production.

docs.title: Audit trail
docs.text: An admin API whose sensitive actions leave an audit trail: who changed which account's role or deleted it, whether they were allowed to, and the request it came from. FastAPIAudit writes each event when the endpoint ends, as a line of JSON on standard output, signed and chained to the previous one, and verify_audit_trail checks that none was altered or removed.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.audit.main:app

The events are signed: set AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process, and keep it from the people whose actions are recorded. The example has three accounts: u1 (Ada, an admin, token ada-token), u2 (Sam, support, token sam-token) and u3 (Vic, a viewer).

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Ada makes Vic support:

$ curl -i -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/accounts/u3/role -H "Authorization: Bearer ada-token" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"role": "support"}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-request-id: 2b78a9c373054722779a26e2904a6b0a

{"id":"u3","email":"vic@example.com","role":"support"}

and the server's standard output gets the event, the request's ID included:

{"id":"eec01d5969ce42deb8787aae473acfa1","time":"2026-10-26T15:44:27.175075+00:00","action":"account.role.change","outcome":"success","actor":"u1","resource":"account:u3","reason":null,"status":null,"request_id":"2b78a9c373054722779a26e2904a6b0a","trace_id":null,"method":"PUT","route":"/accounts/{account_id}/role","client":"127.0.0.1","details":{"from":"viewer","to":"support"},"stream":"1c33125463a71ecb","sequence":1,"previous":null,"signature":"13c0da20bf320784d6a1a4698cd91574b2b97b8c8e818668ef104aa9cc65fb34"}

Sam, who isn't an admin, tries to delete Vic's account; then someone without a token does:

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8000/accounts/u3 -H "Authorization: Bearer sam-token"
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

{"detail":"Only admins can do this"}

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8000/accounts/u3
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

Both are recorded as denied: Sam's with who he is and why, the anonymous one with the account it was after. Each event carries the signature of the one before:

{"id":"2221174595b04a82b269e441227a0933","time":"2026-10-26T15:44:27.178638+00:00","action":"account.delete","outcome":"denied","actor":"u2","resource":"account:u3","reason":"support, not admin","status":403,"request_id":"14500c6bd67ff72fd772d584cdb9fee5","trace_id":null,"method":"DELETE","route":"/accounts/{account_id}","client":"127.0.0.1","details":{},"stream":"1c33125463a71ecb","sequence":2,"previous":"13c0da20bf320784d6a1a4698cd91574b2b97b8c8e818668ef104aa9cc65fb34","signature":"41ea75d99c58cd8618d1f3e5bad140e52f270929beb26cc811a53c9bee452aa6"}
{"id":"41a26fffb4bd41df9d8c370da2d9cc7d","time":"2026-10-26T15:44:27.182414+00:00","action":"account.delete","outcome":"denied","actor":null,"resource":"account:u3","reason":"fastapi.exceptions.HTTPException","status":401,"request_id":"028f8c3e03768e47f6f85152ba18cf48","trace_id":null,"method":"DELETE","route":"/accounts/{account_id}","client":"127.0.0.1","details":{},"stream":"1c33125463a71ecb","sequence":3,"previous":"41ea75d99c58cd8618d1f3e5bad140e52f270929beb26cc811a53c9bee452aa6","signature":"be3d2ff3bb03a6642e81027d5ac0edc75356ab880f9434b2ba88a089ff91eda5"}

A sign-in with a wrong password records which account was tried, never the password:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/sessions -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "ada@example.com", "password": "hunter2"}'
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
x-request-id: b544c2688f7bd5b8cc1c58784a44ca68

{"detail":"Wrong e-mail or password"}

{"id":"6c10e3d17e1d4e3d9442c181ebc6e525","time":"2026-10-26T15:44:27.185776+00:00","action":"session.create","outcome":"denied","actor":"u1","resource":null,"reason":"wrong password","status":null,"request_id":"b544c2688f7bd5b8cc1c58784a44ca68","trace_id":null,"method":"POST","route":"/sessions","client":"127.0.0.1","details":{},"stream":"1c33125463a71ecb","sequence":4,"previous":"be3d2ff3bb03a6642e81027d5ac0edc75356ab880f9434b2ba88a089ff91eda5","signature":"9124fbfed7d210bde4fe27842947404b9c711d86acd3b6e1469e0af09d97c7d0"}

Ada checks the trail (and that check is recorded too, as audit.read). An event altered, forged or removed would be listed in problems:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/audit/verify -H "Authorization: Bearer ada-token"
{"events":4,"problems":[]}

GET /audit/events lists the last events, for admins only.

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The audit dependency comes first: declared before current_account, it's entered before the authentication runs, so the 401s that one answers are recorded too, with the account from the path (resource="account:{account_id}").
  • Who acts goes in before the check: require_admin sets entry.actor and then refuses, so Sam's 403 is recorded with Sam, and entry.reason says why.
  • How it ended: a 401 or a 403 is denied, any other exception a failure (a 404 for an account that doesn't exist), with its type and status but never its message.
  • No secrets: the sign-in records the account and the reason, not the e-mail address typed (it may be a password typed in the wrong field) nor the password. Had they gone in details, the password would have been [redacted], by its key.
  • A stream of its own: the events go to the logger fastapi_alcazaba.audit.events, which writes them to standard output without the app's log format, one line each, for the log pipeline to ship to storage that can't be rewritten (an S3 bucket with Object Lock, a SIEM).
  • Signed and chained: each event carries an HMAC of its content and the signature of the previous one of its process. verify_audit_trail finds an event altered, forged or missing in the middle; it can't tell that the newest were removed, nor stop whoever has the key.
  • Correlation: the x-request-id a user quotes leads to the event (request_id), and with OpenTelemetry the event's trace_id leads to the request's trace.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/audit/main.py
"""An admin API whose sensitive actions leave an audit trail: who did what to which account,
whether it was allowed, and the request it came from.

    uvicorn examples.audit.main:app

- Changing a role and deleting an account are recorded when they end: `success`, `denied` (a 401
  without a token, a 403 for someone who isn't an admin) or `failure` (a 404 for an account that
  doesn't exist). Reading the trail is recorded too.
- Each event is a line of JSON on standard output, apart from the app's other logs, for the log
  pipeline to ship to storage that can't be rewritten. The events are signed and chained:
  `GET /audit/verify` says whether any was altered or removed.
- A sign-in records its outcome with `audit.log`, never the password, and the response carries
  the request ID that the event holds.

The accounts are a dict in memory here, a table in your database; the last events are kept in
memory too, for `/audit/events` and `/audit/verify`.
"""

import hmac
import logging
import secrets
import sys
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Any, Literal

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
from starlette.requests import HTTPConnection

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPIAudit
from fastapi_alcazaba.audit import AuditEntry, LoggingAuditSink, MemoryAuditSink, verify_audit_trail
from fastapi_alcazaba.observability import RequestIDMiddleware


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    # Signs the events: AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process,
    # kept from the people whose actions are recorded: with it, they could rewrite the trail.
    audit_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()

# The trail: one line of JSON per event on standard output, without the app's log format.
trail_log = logging.getLogger("fastapi_alcazaba.audit.events")
trail_log.addHandler(logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout))
trail_log.setLevel(logging.INFO)
trail_log.propagate = False

recent = MemoryAuditSink(maxlen=1000)
audit = FastAPIAudit([LoggingAuditSink(trail_log), recent], signing_key=settings.audit_signing_key)

Role = Literal["admin", "support", "viewer"]


class Account(BaseModel):
    id: str
    email: str
    role: Role


class RoleChange(BaseModel):
    role: Role


class SignIn(BaseModel):
    email: str
    password: str


# Stands in for your users table, its password hashes and your access tokens.
PASSWORDS = {"ada@example.com": "correct horse", "sam@example.com": "battery staple"}
TOKENS = {"ada-token": "u1", "sam-token": "u2"}


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    application.state.accounts = {
        "u1": Account(id="u1", email="ada@example.com", role="admin"),
        "u2": Account(id="u2", email="sam@example.com", role="support"),
        "u3": Account(id="u3", email="vic@example.com", role="viewer"),
    }
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
# The ID of each request goes in its events and in the response: support finds the event a
# user's complaint is about.
app.add_middleware(RequestIDMiddleware)


def accounts(request: Request) -> dict[str, Account]:
    return request.app.state.accounts  # type: ignore[no-any-return]


Accounts = Annotated[dict[str, Account], Depends(accounts)]


async def current_account(connection: HTTPConnection) -> Account:
    """Stands in for your authentication: the account whose bearer token the request carries."""
    scheme, _, token = connection.headers.get("authorization", "").partition(" ")
    account_id = TOKENS.get(token) if scheme.lower() == "bearer" else None
    account = connection.app.state.accounts.get(account_id)
    if account is None:
        raise HTTPException(401, "Not authenticated", headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
    return account  # type: ignore[no-any-return]


Me = Annotated[Account, Depends(current_account)]


def require_admin(entry: AuditEntry, me: Account) -> None:
    """Who acts goes in the event before the check: a refusal is recorded with its actor."""
    entry.actor = me.id
    if me.role != "admin":
        entry.reason = f"{me.role}, not admin"
        raise HTTPException(403, "Only admins can do this")


def find(all_accounts: dict[str, Account], account_id: str) -> Account:
    account = all_accounts.get(account_id)
    if account is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such account")
    return account


# The audit dependency goes before the authentication (Me): it records what that one refuses,
# a 401, with the account from the path.
changing_role = audit.action("account.role.change", resource="account:{account_id}")
deleting = audit.action("account.delete", resource="account:{account_id}")
reading_trail = audit.action("audit.read")


@app.put("/accounts/{account_id}/role")
async def change_role(
    account_id: str,
    change: RoleChange,
    entry: Annotated[AuditEntry, Depends(changing_role)],
    me: Me,
    all_accounts: Accounts,
) -> Account:
    require_admin(entry, me)
    account = find(all_accounts, account_id)
    entry.details.update({"from": account.role, "to": change.role})
    account.role = change.role
    return account


@app.delete("/accounts/{account_id}", status_code=204)
async def delete_account(
    account_id: str,
    entry: Annotated[AuditEntry, Depends(deleting)],
    me: Me,
    all_accounts: Accounts,
) -> None:
    require_admin(entry, me)
    entry.details["email"] = find(all_accounts, account_id).email
    del all_accounts[account_id]


@app.post("/sessions")
async def sign_in(form: SignIn, request: Request, all_accounts: Accounts) -> dict[str, str]:
    account = next((a for a in all_accounts.values() if a.email == form.email), None)
    expected = PASSWORDS.get(form.email, "")
    # Compared in constant time, and the same answer whatever was wrong.
    if account is None or not hmac.compare_digest(form.password.encode(), expected.encode()):
        await audit.log(
            "session.create",
            outcome="denied",
            actor=account.id if account else None,
            reason="unknown e-mail" if account is None else "wrong password",
            request=request,
        )
        raise HTTPException(401, "Wrong e-mail or password")
    await audit.log("session.create", actor=account.id, request=request)
    token = next(token for token, owner in TOKENS.items() if owner == account.id)
    return {"access_token": token, "token_type": "bearer"}


@app.get("/audit/events")
async def audit_events(
    entry: Annotated[AuditEntry, Depends(reading_trail)],
    me: Me,
    limit: int = 20,
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    require_admin(entry, me)
    return [event.to_dict() for event in list(recent.events)[-limit:]]


@app.get("/audit/verify")
async def audit_verify(
    entry: Annotated[AuditEntry, Depends(reading_trail)],
    me: Me,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    require_admin(entry, me)
    events = list(recent.events)
    return {
        "events": len(events),
        "problems": verify_audit_trail(events, settings.audit_signing_key),
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: API keys, revoked tokens and one-time codes
docs.text:
An orders API for machine clients. Their owners sign in with a code sent by e-mail (OneTimeCodes), rate-limited per address with a FastAPIRateLimiter, and get an access token that logging out revokes (TokenBlocklist). With it they create API keys for their programs (FastAPIAPIKeys): shown once, stored only as digests, with scopes and an expiry date.

No JWT library is involved: a small stand-in signs the same claims (sub, jti, iat, exp) with HMAC. A real app decodes its JWTs with its library and passes the blocklist the same claims.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.auth.main:app

Set CACHE_SIGNING_KEY, OTP_SECRET, API_KEY_PEPPER and TOKEN_SECRET (secrets.token_urlsafe(32) each), the same in every process. Without them each start makes up throwaway ones, and every token, code and key stops working when the app restarts.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Ask for a code. The answer is the same whether the address has an account or not:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/login/code -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "ana@example.com"}'
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted

{"detail":"If the address has an account, a code is on its way."}

The code never travels in a response. The stand-in for the e-mail service prints it in the server's terminal:

E-mail to ana@example.com: Your login code is 531060. It expires in 5 minutes.

Trade it for an access token. It works once:

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "ana@example.com", "code": "531060"}'
{"access_token":"eyJzdWIiOiJhbmFAZXhhbXBsZS5jb20i...","expires_in":900}

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "ana@example.com", "code": "531060"}'
{"detail":"Invalid or expired code"}

Three codes per address every 15 minutes, wherever the requests come from. The fourth:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/login/code -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "ben@example.com"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
retry-after: 558

{"detail":"Too Many Requests"}

With the token, create two API keys, one that can only read. Each key is shown this once:

$ TOKEN=eyJzdWIiOiJhbmFAZXhhbXBsZS5jb20i...
$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api-keys -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"scopes": ["orders:read"]}'
{"id":"j2aelpaafvjfr6ry","key":"acme_j2aelpaafvjfr6ry_gqdbzjcgz6dwuwtbmltalhn7cern6vjogztxgthxqwofrt6z2aaa","scopes":["orders:read"],"expires_at":"2027-01-24T10:55:42.303928Z"}

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api-keys -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"scopes": ["orders:read", "orders:write"]}'
{"id":"mxkvocavyp6ek2dc","key":"acme_mxkvocavyp6ek2dc_hnkk5z2qld3qoc7wv5sq2aq4qrvblr7mc4bucwfvbzj5uzea6d5a","scopes":["orders:read","orders:write"],"expires_at":"2027-01-24T10:55:42.306965Z"}

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api-keys -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"scopes": ["admin"]}'
{"detail":[{"type":"enum","loc":["body","scopes",0],"msg":"Input should be 'orders:read' or 'orders:write'",...}]}

Each endpoint asks for the scope it needs:

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "X-API-Key: acme_mxkvocavyp6ek2dc_hnkk5z2qld3qoc7wv5sq2aq4qrvblr7mc4bucwfvbzj5uzea6d5a" \
    -d '{"item": "Olive oil", "quantity": 2}'
{"item":"Olive oil","quantity":2}

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "X-API-Key: acme_j2aelpaafvjfr6ry_gqdbzjcgz6dwuwtbmltalhn7cern6vjogztxgthxqwofrt6z2aaa" \
    -d '{"item": "Olive oil", "quantity": 2}'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

{"detail":"Insufficient scope"}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders \
    -H "X-API-Key: acme_j2aelpaafvjfr6ry_gqdbzjcgz6dwuwtbmltalhn7cern6vjogztxgthxqwofrt6z2aaa"
[{"item":"Olive oil","quantity":2}]

A missing, malformed, unknown, wrong or expired key gets the same 401:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "X-API-Key: acme_nottherightkey"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: APIKey

{"detail":"Invalid API key"}

Revoking a key takes effect at once in the process that handles it:

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8000/api-keys/j2aelpaafvjfr6ry -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders \
    -H "X-API-Key: acme_j2aelpaafvjfr6ry_gqdbzjcgz6dwuwtbmltalhn7cern6vjogztxgthxqwofrt6z2aaa"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: APIKey

{"detail":"Invalid API key"}

Logging out revokes the access token, which would otherwise work for 15 minutes more:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/logout -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/logout -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Invalid or expired token"}

/logout/everywhere revokes every token of the user issued before the current second, and gives the session that asked a new one. With two tokens of Ana's, $LAPTOP and $PHONE, issued a second or more before:

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/logout/everywhere -H "Authorization: Bearer $PHONE"
{"access_token":"eyJzdWIiOiJhbmFAZXhhbXBsZS5jb20i...","expires_in":900}

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api-keys \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LAPTOP" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"scopes": ["orders:read"]}'
401

$PHONE gets a 401 as well, and the new token a 201.

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Nothing that opens a door is stored in clear: the api_keys table holds an HMAC of each key with the pepper, which lives outside the database, so a copy of the database can't even test a guess. The cache's backend holds HMACs of the codes and digests of the revoked token ids.
  • The code only goes by e-mail, and /login/code answers the same for any address. The e-mail is sent after the response (BackgroundTasks), so the time it takes doesn't tell either.
  • The rate limit on codes is per address, wherever the requests come from (identifier returns the same for everybody; the address is the key of hit). Each new code replaces the previous one and its five guesses, so this limit is what bounds the guesses at an account: 3 codes × 5 guesses every 15 minutes.
  • The token check is one dependency, token_claims: it decodes the token and asks the blocklist with its jti, and with its sub and iat for /logout/everywhere. With a JWT library you only change the decoding; set the blocklist's leeway to the one your library tolerates after exp.
  • Revoking a key deletes its row and calls keys.forget(), because cache_ttl=30 keeps looked-up records in each process: the other processes stop accepting it within 30 seconds.
  • Scopes are an enum: users can only grant their keys scopes the API knows.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/auth/main.py
"""An orders API for machine clients, whose owners sign in with a code sent by e-mail.

    uvicorn examples.auth.main:app

People sign in with a one-time code (`OneTimeCodes`) and get an access token, which logging out
revokes (`TokenBlocklist`). With it they create API keys (`FastAPIAPIKeys`) for their programs:
shown once, stored as digests, with scopes and an expiry date. The programs call `/orders` with
the key in `X-API-Key`.

Revoked tokens, codes and rate-limit counters live in the cache's backend: in memory here, Redis
or Valkey in production, so that every process sees them at once. Set CACHE_SIGNING_KEY,
OTP_SECRET, API_KEY_PEPPER and TOKEN_SECRET (secrets.token_urlsafe(32) each), the same in every
process, in the environment or a .env file.
"""

import base64
import dataclasses
import hmac
import secrets
import time
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import BackgroundTasks, Body, Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPIAPIKeys, FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth import OneTimeCodes, TokenBlocklist
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.rate_limit import FastAPIRateLimiter, too_many_requests

TOKEN_LIFETIME = 15 * 60  # seconds


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file: secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    each, the same in every process."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    otp_secret: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    api_key_pepper: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    token_secret: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()


class Scope(StrEnum):
    # An enum: users can only grant scopes the API knows.
    ORDERS_READ = "orders:read"
    ORDERS_WRITE = "orders:write"


@dataclasses.dataclass
class APIKeyRow:
    """A row of the api_keys table: everything about a key but the key itself."""

    id: str
    owner: str
    digest: str
    scopes: frozenset[str]
    expires_at: datetime | None


class Order(BaseModel):
    item: str = Field(max_length=100)
    quantity: int = Field(ge=1, le=100)


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users = {"ana@example.com", "ben@example.com"}
        self.api_keys: dict[str, APIKeyRow] = {}
        self.orders: dict[str, list[Order]] = {}  # by owner


async def send_email(to: str, text: str) -> None:
    """Stands in for the e-mail service: prints the message, for you to read the code in the
    server's terminal, and keeps it for the tests."""
    outbox.append((to, text))
    print(f"E-mail to {to}: {text}", flush=True)


class Claims(BaseModel):
    sub: str
    jti: str
    iat: int
    exp: int


class AccessTokens:
    """Stands in for a JWT library, which this example doesn't depend on: a JWT's claims, signed
    with HMAC-SHA256. A real app issues and decodes its JWTs with PyJWT or joserfc, and gives the
    blocklist their `jti`, `sub`, `iat` and `exp` just like here."""

    def __init__(self, key: SecretStr) -> None:
        self.key = key.get_secret_value().encode()

    def sign(self, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
        return hmac.digest(self.key, payload, "sha256").hex().encode()

    def issue(self, subject: str) -> str:
        now = int(time.time())
        jti = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
        claims = Claims(sub=subject, jti=jti, iat=now, exp=now + TOKEN_LIFETIME)
        payload = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(claims.model_dump_json().encode())
        return (payload + b"." + self.sign(payload)).decode()

    def decode(self, token: str) -> Claims | None:
        """The claims of a token signed here that hasn't expired; None otherwise."""
        payload, _, signature = token.encode().partition(b".")
        if not hmac.compare_digest(signature, self.sign(payload)):
            return None
        claims = Claims.model_validate_json(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(payload))
        return claims if claims.exp > time.time() else None


db = Database()
outbox: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
access_tokens = AccessTokens(settings.token_secret)
blocklist = TokenBlocklist()  # in FastAPICache's backend
codes = OneTimeCodes(secret=settings.otp_secret)  # 6 digits, 5 minutes, 5 guesses
# Per address, wherever the requests come from. Each code replaces the previous one and its
# guesses, so this is what bounds the guesses at an account: 3 codes x 5 guesses per 15 minutes.
code_requests = FastAPIRateLimiter(times=3, minutes=15, identifier=lambda _: "")


async def load_key(key_id: str) -> APIKeyRow | None:
    return db.api_keys.get(key_id)


# A distinctive prefix, for secret scanners to spot leaked keys. Each process keeps the records
# it looked up for 30 s: a revocation takes up to that long to reach the other processes.
keys = FastAPIAPIKeys(load_key, pepper=settings.api_key_pepper, prefix="acme", cache_ttl=30)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares the state. Signed: revocations
    # planted in the backend are ignored.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="auth", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key)
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
bearer = HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)


async def token_claims(
    credentials: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None, Depends(bearer)],
) -> Claims:
    """The claims of the request's access token; a 401 if it's missing, expired or revoked."""
    claims = access_tokens.decode(credentials.credentials) if credentials else None
    if claims is None or await blocklist.is_revoked(
        claims.jti, subject=claims.sub, issued_at=claims.iat
    ):
        raise HTTPException(401, "Invalid or expired token", headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
    return claims


TokenClaims = Annotated[Claims, Depends(token_claims)]


class CodeRequest(BaseModel):
    email: str = Field(max_length=254)


class Login(CodeRequest):
    code: str = Field(max_length=10)


class Token(BaseModel):
    access_token: str
    expires_in: int = TOKEN_LIFETIME


@app.post("/login/code", status_code=status.HTTP_202_ACCEPTED)
async def send_code(form: CodeRequest, request: Request, tasks: BackgroundTasks) -> dict[str, str]:
    """E-mail a login code. The answer doesn't tell whether the address has an account."""
    email = form.email.lower()
    if (wait := await code_requests.hit(request, key=email)) is not None:
        too_many_requests(request, wait)
    tasks.add_task(email_code, email)  # after the response: its timing doesn't tell either
    return {"detail": "If the address has an account, a code is on its way."}


async def email_code(email: str) -> None:
    if email in db.users:
        code = await codes.issue(email, purpose="login")
        await send_email(email, f"Your login code is {code}. It expires in 5 minutes.")


@app.post("/login")
async def login(form: Login) -> Token:
    email = form.email.lower()
    if not await codes.verify(email, form.code, purpose="login"):
        raise HTTPException(400, "Invalid or expired code")
    return Token(access_token=access_tokens.issue(email))


@app.post("/logout", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def logout(claims: TokenClaims) -> None:
    """Refuse this token from now on, until it would have expired anyway."""
    await blocklist.revoke(claims.jti, expires_at=claims.exp)


@app.post("/logout/everywhere")
async def logout_everywhere(claims: TokenClaims) -> Token:
    """Refuse every token of the user issued before this second (a lost laptop, a new password),
    and give this session a new one, which stays valid."""
    await blocklist.revoke_subject(claims.sub, ttl=TOKEN_LIFETIME)
    return Token(access_token=access_tokens.issue(claims.sub))


class NewKey(BaseModel):
    id: str
    key: str
    scopes: list[str]
    expires_at: datetime | None


@app.post("/api-keys", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def create_key(
    claims: TokenClaims,
    scopes: Annotated[set[Scope], Body(embed=True, min_length=1)],
) -> NewKey:
    """A new key, shown this once: only a digest of it is stored."""
    expires_at = datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=90)
    key, record = keys.generate(scopes=scopes, expires_at=expires_at)
    db.api_keys[record.id] = APIKeyRow(owner=claims.sub, **dataclasses.asdict(record))
    return NewKey(id=record.id, key=key, scopes=sorted(scopes), expires_at=expires_at)


@app.delete("/api-keys/{key_id}", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def revoke_key(key_id: str, claims: TokenClaims) -> None:
    row = db.api_keys.get(key_id)
    if row is None or row.owner != claims.sub:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such key")
    del db.api_keys[key_id]
    keys.forget(key_id)  # refused at once by this process, by the others within cache_ttl


@app.get("/orders")
async def list_orders(
    key: Annotated[APIKeyRow, Depends(keys.require(Scope.ORDERS_READ))],
) -> list[Order]:
    return db.orders.get(key.owner, [])


@app.post("/orders", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def add_order(
    order: Order,
    key: Annotated[APIKeyRow, Depends(keys.require(Scope.ORDERS_WRITE))],
) -> Order:
    db.orders.setdefault(key.owner, []).append(order)
    return order


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: Background work
docs.text:
A sign-up service whose work goes on after the response. POST /users saves the user and hands the welcome e-mail to FastAPITaskQueue, which runs it in the background, in whichever process takes it, and retries it while the e-mail provider is down. Out of retries, it becomes a dead letter, which an admin endpoint lists and puts back in the queue once the provider is back. FastAPIScheduler ends the trials on the hour and sends the team a sign-up report on weekdays at 8:00 in Madrid, each run in one process only.
