And FastAPILeader has one process relay the outbox, the events saved with the users, to the message broker; if that process stops, another one takes over.

Unlike the other examples, it needs Redis or Valkey: the tasks live in Redis streams that every process shares. They're signed with the cache's signing_key, so a task planted or altered in Redis is refused and never runs.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository, with Redis or Valkey running (a throwaway one: docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:6379:6379 valkey/valkey:8):

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
export REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0
export CACHE_SIGNING_KEY=$(python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))")
export ADMIN_TOKEN=$(python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))")
uvicorn examples.background.main:app

Every process needs the same CACHE_SIGNING_KEY, or the tasks that one seals are refused by the others. The admin routes take Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN; without ADMIN_TOKEN the token is random, and they stay closed. The database, the e-mail provider and the broker are stand-ins in the process's memory, so try it with one process. With a real database, run as many as you need.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
A sign-up answers at once, before the welcome e-mail goes out. A moment later the queue has sent it:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/users -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "ana@example.com", "name": "Ana"}'
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json

{"id":1,"email":"ana@example.com","name":"Ana","created_at":"2026-10-26T11:36:58.884780Z","plan":"trial","welcomed":false}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/users/1
{"id":1,"email":"ana@example.com","name":"Ana","created_at":"2026-10-26T11:36:58.884780Z","plan":"trial","welcomed":true}

What the process is doing: it's the leader, no task is pending, and the jobs run next (in UTC) on the hour and at 8:00 in Madrid, which is 7:00 UTC in winter time. Without the token, a 401:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/background -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
{"leader":true,"pending_tasks":0,"next_runs":{"end-trials":"2026-10-26T12:00:00Z","signup-report":"2026-10-27T07:00:00Z"}}

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/background
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

Now the e-mail provider goes down. A sign-up still answers at once, and its task waits for a retry:

$ curl -X PUT "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/simulate/mailer?down=true" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/users -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "luis@example.com", "name": "Luis"}'
{"id":2,"email":"luis@example.com","name":"Luis","created_at":"2026-10-26T11:36:59.914617Z","plan":"trial","welcomed":false}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/background -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
{"leader":true,"pending_tasks":1,"next_runs":{"end-trials":"2026-10-26T12:00:00Z","signup-report":"2026-10-27T07:00:00Z"}}

The retries come 10 s, 20 s, 40 s… apart, with jitter. After the sixth attempt, here about four minutes later, the task is a dead letter. It says which task failed and the type of its error, never its arguments nor the error's message, which may hold personal data:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/dead-letters -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
[{"id":"1793014866323-0","reason":"failed","task":"send-welcome-email","task_id":"dd4b818df71444c0af26dcc01e59ce10","error":"examples.background.main.MailerUnavailable","attempts":6,"failed_at":"2026-10-26T11:41:06.323669Z"}]

Once the provider is back, the dead letter goes back in the queue, and the e-mail goes out:

$ curl -X PUT "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/simulate/mailer?down=false" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/dead-letters/requeue \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
{"requeued":1}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/users/2
{"id":2,"email":"luis@example.com","name":"Luis","created_at":"2026-10-26T11:36:59.914617Z","plan":"trial","welcomed":true}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/dead-letters -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
[]

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• At least once, so safe to run twice: a worker that dies after sending the e-mail, before it can say so, has its task run again elsewhere. send_welcome_email checks first whether the e-mail already went out.
  • Only an ID goes through Redis: the task takes the user's ID and reads the address when it runs, so no personal data waits in Redis, and the log line names the user by ID too.
  • Sealed tasks: the cache's signing_key signs every task and binds it to its queue. Without it, whoever can write to Redis could run the tasks with arguments of their choosing.
  • Each run in one process: the scheduler's ticks are the same in every process (every(hours=1) is on the hour, UTC), and only one of them runs each tick. The cron job has a time zone, so the report is at 8:00 in Madrid in summer time and in winter time.
  • One relay, never two: two processes relaying the outbox would publish every event twice. The leader's loop is cancelled if its process stops leading, and starts in the next leader. An event leaves the outbox only once it's published: a crash in between publishes it again, and never loses it.
  • Started and stopped with the app: async with queue, leader, scheduler in the lifespan. They stop in the reverse order: the jobs first, the queue last, giving its running tasks 10 s.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/background/main.py
"""Background work for a sign-up service: a task queue, scheduled jobs and a leader, on Redis.

    export REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0
    export CACHE_SIGNING_KEY=$(python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))")
    export ADMIN_TOKEN=$(python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))")
    uvicorn examples.background.main:app

Every process runs the three tools, started and stopped with the app, and they share the work
through Redis: in production, run as many processes as you need (`--workers`, more machines).
Here the database is a stand-in in each process's memory, so try it with one.

- FastAPITaskQueue: POST /users hands the welcome e-mail to the queue, which retries it while the
  e-mail provider is down. After its last retry it's a dead letter, which the admin endpoints
  list and put back in the queue once the provider is back.
- FastAPIScheduler: trials end on the hour, and the team gets a sign-up report on weekdays at
  8:00 in Madrid; each run happens in one process only.
- FastAPILeader: one process relays the outbox (the events saved with the users) to the message
  broker; if it stops, another one takes over.

The e-mail provider is a stand-in too: `PUT /admin/simulate/mailer?down=true` makes it fail, to
watch retries and dead letters. The admin routes take `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN`. The
variables above can go in a .env file instead.
"""

import asyncio
import logging
import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Annotated, Any

import uvicorn
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
from redis.asyncio import Redis

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache, FastAPILeader, FastAPIScheduler, FastAPITaskQueue
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.redis import RedisBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.background import DeadLetter

logger = logging.getLogger("signup")


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    redis_url: str = "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0"  # rediss://, with a password, in production
    # Every process needs the same key, or the tasks one seals are refused by the others. The
    # random default only suits a single process that you try out locally.
    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    # Unset: a random token nobody knows, so the admin endpoints stay closed.
    admin_token: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()
REPORT_TO = "team@example.com"
TRIAL = timedelta(days=14)
RELAY_INTERVAL = 1.0  # seconds between looks at the outbox


def redis_client() -> Redis:
    """The connection to Redis or Valkey."""
    return Redis.from_url(settings.redis_url)


class MailerUnavailable(Exception):
    """The e-mail provider didn't answer."""


class Mailer:
    """Stands in for the e-mail provider's client."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.available = True
        self.sent: list[tuple[str, str]] = []  # (to, subject)

    async def send(self, to: str, subject: str) -> None:
        if not self.available:
            raise MailerUnavailable("503 Service Unavailable")
        self.sent.append((to, subject))


@dataclass
class User:
    id: int
    email: str
    name: str
    created_at: datetime
    plan: str = "trial"
    welcomed: bool = False


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database, which every process shares in a real app."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users: dict[int, User] = {}
        self.outbox: list[dict[str, Any]] = []  # events, saved in the same transaction as the data

    def add_user(self, email: str, name: str, created_at: datetime | None = None) -> User:
        user = User(len(self.users) + 1, email, name, created_at or datetime.now(UTC))
        self.users[user.id] = user
        self.outbox.append({"type": "user.created", "user_id": user.id})
        return user


class Broker:
    """Stands in for the message broker (Kafka, RabbitMQ...)."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.published: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    async def publish(self, event: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        self.published.append(event)


db, mailer, broker = Database(), Mailer(), Broker()
# FastAPICache's backend, set in the lifespan.
queue = FastAPITaskQueue()
scheduler = FastAPIScheduler()
leader = FastAPILeader("outbox-relay")


# Six attempts over about five minutes (10 s, 20 s, 40 s... apart, with jitter), then a dead letter.
@queue.task(name="send-welcome-email", retries=5, backoff=10)
async def send_welcome_email(user_id: int) -> None:
    """Runs at least once, so it checks first whether the e-mail already went out."""
    user = db.users.get(user_id)
    if user is None or user.welcomed:  # deleted meanwhile, or a second run
        return
    await mailer.send(user.email, f"Welcome, {user.name}!")
    user.welcomed = True
    logger.info("Welcome e-mail sent to user %d", user_id)  # an ID, not the address


@scheduler.every(hours=1, name="end-trials")
async def end_trials() -> None:
    """On the hour (UTC): the users whose trial is over go to the free plan."""
    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    for user in db.users.values():
        if user.plan == "trial" and user.created_at + TRIAL <= now:
            user.plan = "free"


@scheduler.cron("0 8 * * mon-fri", tz="Europe/Madrid", name="signup-report")
async def signup_report() -> None:
    """Weekdays at 8:00 in Madrid, in summer time and in winter time."""
    since = datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(days=1)
    count = sum(user.created_at >= since for user in db.users.values())
    await mailer.send(REPORT_TO, f"{count} sign-ups in the last 24 hours")


@leader.run
async def relay_outbox() -> None:
    """In the leader only: two processes would publish every event twice. It's cancelled if this
    process stops leading, and starts again in the next leader."""
    while True:
        while db.outbox:
            await broker.publish(db.outbox[0])
            db.outbox.pop(0)  # once it's out: a crash in between publishes it again, never loses it
        await asyncio.sleep(RELAY_INTERVAL)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    redis = redis_client()
    # Signed: a task planted or altered in Redis is refused and never runs.
    FastAPICache.init(RedisBackend(redis), prefix="signup", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key)
    # Stopped in the reverse order: the jobs first, the queue last, giving its running tasks 10 s.
    async with queue, leader, scheduler:
        yield
    await redis.aclose()


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


class SignUp(BaseModel):
    email: str = Field(max_length=254, pattern=r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+$")
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)


@app.post("/users", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def sign_up(signup: SignUp) -> User:
    """The response doesn't wait for the e-mail provider, nor fails while it's down."""
    user = db.add_user(signup.email, signup.name)
    # Only the ID goes through Redis: no personal data there, and the task reads the address then.
    await queue.enqueue(send_welcome_email, user.id)
    return user


@app.get("/users/{user_id}")
async def get_user(user_id: int) -> User:
    if (user := db.users.get(user_id)) is None:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND)
    return user


def require_admin(
    credentials: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, Depends(HTTPBearer())],
) -> None:
    if not secrets.compare_digest(
        credentials.credentials.encode(), settings.admin_token.get_secret_value().encode()
    ):
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN)


admin = APIRouter(prefix="/admin", dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)])


class Background(BaseModel):
    leader: bool
    pending_tasks: int
    next_runs: dict[str, datetime | None]


@admin.get("/background")
async def background() -> Background:
    """Whether this process leads, the tasks not done yet and when the jobs run next (UTC)."""
    return Background(
        leader=leader.is_leader,
        pending_tasks=await queue.pending(),
        next_runs={name: scheduler.next_run(name) for name in ("end-trials", "signup-report")},
    )


@admin.get("/dead-letters")
async def dead_letters() -> list[DeadLetter]:
    """The tasks out of retries, newest first: their name and error type, never their arguments."""
    return await queue.dead_letters()


@admin.post("/dead-letters/requeue")
async def requeue_dead_letters() -> dict[str, int]:
    """Once the cause is fixed: every dead letter back in the queue, with its attempts reset."""
    return {"requeued": await queue.requeue_dead_letters()}


@admin.put("/simulate/mailer", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def simulate_mailer(down: bool) -> None:
    """Only in this example: makes the e-mail provider fail, to watch retries and dead letters."""
    mailer.available = not down


app.include_router(admin)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: A browser app: sessions, CSRF and security headers
docs.text: A small shop rendered on the server, with plain HTML and a few lines of JavaScript. Who signed in and the cart live in a server-side session (ServerSessionMiddleware): the cookie only carries a random id, which signing in replaces and signing out deletes, and 30 minutes without requests end it. CSRFMiddleware refuses what pages on other sites make the browser send, and with require_token=True also wants the page's token in a header. SecurityHeadersMiddleware and BodySizeLimitMiddleware add the security headers, with a Content-Security-Policy for the pages, and refuse large bodies. A FastAPIRateLimiter slows down password guessing.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.browser_app.main:app

Open http://localhost:8000 and sign in as ana, password correct horse battery staple.

The cookies are Secure: browsers only keep them from HTTPS sites and from http://localhost, which they treat as secure. Use localhost, not a LAN address, to try it over plain HTTP. In tests, give the client an https URL for the same reason: TestClient(app, base_url="https://testserver").

Set SESSION_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process. Without it each start makes up a throwaway one, and every session ends when the app restarts.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
curl keeps Secure cookies from localhost too, so a cookie jar plays the browser. The first page sets the CSRF token, in a cookie and in the page, and carries the security headers:

$ curl -i -c jar -b jar http://localhost:8000/
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8
vary: Cookie
set-cookie: __Host-csrftoken=QkgoLDXsFG6SGZsxRY39XJJJWKwuVB1VQCAoC7HQIpc; Path=/; Secure; SameSite=Lax
x-content-type-options: nosniff
x-frame-options: DENY
referrer-policy: no-referrer
cross-origin-opener-policy: same-origin
content-security-policy: default-src 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'

<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Shop</title><meta name="csrf-token" content="QkgoLDXsFG6SGZsxRY39XJJJWKwuVB1VQCAoC7HQIpc"><script src="/app.js" defer></script></head><body><p><a href="/login">Sign in</a></p>...

No session yet: it's only created when there's something to keep. A form posted without the token is refused, even from the app's own page (Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin, as browsers send):

$ curl -i -c jar -b jar -X POST http://localhost:8000/cart -H "Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin" \
    -d product=Figs
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

{"detail":"Missing or invalid CSRF token"}

With the token in X-CSRF-Token, as app.js sends it, the cart gets a session:

$ curl -i -c jar -b jar -X POST http://localhost:8000/cart -H "Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin" \
    -H "X-CSRF-Token: QkgoLDXsFG6SGZsxRY39XJJJWKwuVB1VQCAoC7HQIpc" -d product=Figs
HTTP/1.1 303 See Other
location: /
set-cookie: __Host-session=ozlYn1TlYGLpFmUZlKT0eArPzN2hQZkbFLVVbPWV1II; Max-Age=28800; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax
cache-control: no-store

Signing in gives the session a new id, with the same cart:

$ curl -i -c jar -b jar -X POST http://localhost:8000/login -H "Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin" \
    -H "X-CSRF-Token: QkgoLDXsFG6SGZsxRY39XJJJWKwuVB1VQCAoC7HQIpc" \
    -d username=ana --data-urlencode "password=correct horse battery staple"
HTTP/1.1 303 See Other
location: /
set-cookie: __Host-session=s4wi5n6b_DRAvO0aFKJ7gzK6lyPtWymwDfZ8Xqm8AJ0; Max-Age=28800; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax

$ curl -b jar http://localhost:8000/
...<p>Signed in as ana.</p>...<h2>Cart</h2><ul><li>Figs: 1</li></ul></body></html>

The old id is worth nothing now, so one planted in the browser before signing in (session fixation) gives nothing away:

$ curl http://localhost:8000/ -H "Cookie: __Host-session=ozlYn1TlYGLpFmUZlKT0eArPzN2hQZkbFLVVbPWV1II"
...<p><a href="/login">Sign in</a></p>...

A page on another site can't sign the user out, even if it had the token:

$ curl -i -b jar -X POST http://localhost:8000/logout -H "Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site" \
    -H "Origin: https://evil.example" -H "X-CSRF-Token: QkgoLDXsFG6SGZsxRY39XJJJWKwuVB1VQCAoC7HQIpc"
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
x-frame-options: DENY
content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'

{"detail":"Cross-site request refused"}

Signing out deletes the session from the backend: a copy of the cookie doesn't work either:

$ curl -i -c jar -b jar -X POST http://localhost:8000/logout -H "Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin" \
    -H "X-CSRF-Token: QkgoLDXsFG6SGZsxRY39XJJJWKwuVB1VQCAoC7HQIpc"
HTTP/1.1 303 See Other
location: /
set-cookie: __Host-session=; Max-Age=0; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax

$ curl http://localhost:8000/ -H "Cookie: __Host-session=s4wi5n6b_DRAvO0aFKJ7gzK6lyPtWymwDfZ8Xqm8AJ0"
...<p><a href="/login">Sign in</a></p>...

Bodies over 64 KiB are refused before the app reads them:

$ head -c 100000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' x > big.txt
$ curl -i -b jar -X POST http://localhost:8000/cart --data-binary @big.txt
HTTP/1.1 413 Content Too Large
x-content-type-options: nosniff

{"detail":"Request body too large"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The order of the middlewares: each one added wraps those before it. The session is the innermost; CSRF goes outside it, so a refused request never reads a session from the backend; the security headers are the outermost, so the 403s and 413s of the others get them too.
  • require_token=True needs JavaScript: the middleware reads the token from the X-CSRF-Token header, which a plain HTML form can't set, so app.js sends the forms with fetch, taking the token from the page's <meta> (request.state.csrf_token). An app whose forms must work without JavaScript leaves require_token off: the origin checks alone already stop CSRF in every current browser, login CSRF included.
  • A strict Content-Security-Policy for the pages: only the app's own script, no inline code (so the token goes in a <meta> and the script in its own file), no framing, forms only to the app. The JSON responses keep the default default-src 'none'. /docs is off: a site has no use for it, and its CDN scripts wouldn't pass the policy.
  • rotate_session at sign-in, clear_session at sign-out: the first defeats session fixation, the second makes a stolen cookie worthless at once. The __Host- prefix keeps a sibling subdomain from planting either cookie.
  • Small, escaped sessions: the cart only holds products of an enum, at most 10 of each, so a session can't outgrow max_size; everything that reaches the HTML goes through html.escape.
  • Passwords: a salted scrypt hash, computed in a thread (it's slow on purpose) and for unknown users too, so the time doesn't tell who has an account; five attempts a minute per address.

docs.title: The code
Response cache
docs.text: A shop's catalogue and account pages behind @cache: product pages are the same for everybody and share one entry each, account pages depend on who asks and get entries of their own, an update drops the entries of a product by tag, and get_or_set caches what doesn't fit a decorator. Every entry is signed, so whoever can write to Redis can't plant one.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.cache.main:app

It keeps the entries in memory. To share them between processes, give it a Redis or Valkey and a signing key, the same in every process:

export REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0
export CACHE_SIGNING_KEY=$(python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))")
uvicorn examples.cache.main:app --workers 4

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
The first request computes the page and stores it, the next ones get it from the cache, as the Cache-Status header says, with the seconds the entry has left:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
etag: W/"8a7a39cf30d133a472a8c4f0beca023d"
cache-status: Alcazaba; fwd=miss; stored
cache-control: max-age=600

{"id":1,"name":"Olive oil","price":9.5}

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
etag: W/"8a7a39cf30d133a472a8c4f0beca023d"
cache-status: Alcazaba; hit; ttl=600
cache-control: max-age=600

{"id":1,"name":"Olive oil","price":9.5}

A personal page is cached per Authorization header and marked private, so neither another user nor a shared cache in between gets it:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/me -H "Authorization: Bearer alice"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
cache-status: Alcazaba; fwd=miss; stored
cache-control: private, max-age=30
vary: Authorization, Cookie

{"user":"alice"}

An update drops the product's entry, whatever its key:

$ curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"id": 1, "name": "Olive oil", "price": 10}'
$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/products/1
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
cache-status: Alcazaba; fwd=miss; stored

{"id":1,"name":"Olive oil","price":10.0}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• vary_headers=() only for public data: by default a request with Authorization or Cookie gets an entry of its own, sent as Cache-Control: private. The product page opts out because it's the same for everybody; the account page keeps the default.
  • Tags instead of keys: the product page is tagged product:<id>, so the update drops it (and anything else with that tag) without rebuilding its key.
  • Errors aren't cached: the 404 of an unknown product is computed every time, never replayed.
  • get_or_set for the rest: the recommendations are cached under a key the code chooses, through the same pipeline as the decorator (signing, single flight, locks).
  • A signing key from the environment: the fallback in the code is only for trying it out. With Redis, every process must share the same key, or each refuses the others' entries.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/cache/main.py
"""A shop's catalogue and account pages, cached by Alcazaba.

    uvicorn examples.cache.main:app

With REDIS_URL (redis://localhost:6379/0) the entries live in Redis and every process shares
them; without it, in this process's memory. Either way they're signed: set CACHE_SIGNING_KEY
(secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process.

- `/products/{product_id}`: the same for everybody, one shared entry per product, tagged so that
  an update drops it (and the lists it appears in) without knowing their keys.
- `/me`: depends on who asks. Requests with `Authorization` get entries of their own, sent as
  `Cache-Control: private`, so no user ever gets another's page.
- `/me/recommendations`: `get_or_set`, for what doesn't fit a decorator.
- `exchange_rate`: a plain function cached like an endpoint.
"""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Header, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import Cache, FastAPICache, get_cache
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends import Backend
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.redis import RedisBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.response_cache import cache
from redis import asyncio as aioredis


class Product(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    price: float


class Shop:
    """Stands in for the database, counting the queries that reach it."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.products = {
            1: Product(id=1, name="Olive oil", price=9.5),
            2: Product(id=2, name="Olives", price=3.2),
        }
        self.queries = 0

    def product(self, product_id: int) -> Product | None:
        self.queries += 1
        return self.products.get(product_id)

    def recommendations(self, _user: str) -> list[Product]:
        """The same for everybody here; a real shop would look at the user's history."""
        self.queries += 1
        return list(self.products.values())


shop = Shop()


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    redis_url: str | None = None  # e.g. redis://localhost:6379/0; without it, in memory
    # Throwaway key for trying it out: a real one comes from the environment or a secret
    # manager, and is the same in every process.
    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = SecretStr("development-only-signing-key-0123456")


settings = Settings()


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    url = settings.redis_url
    client = aioredis.from_url(url) if url else None
    backend: Backend = RedisBackend(client) if client is not None else InMemoryBackend()
    FastAPICache.init(
        backend,
        prefix="shop",
        signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key,
    )
    yield
    if client is not None:
        await client.aclose()


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


def current_user(authorization: Annotated[str | None, Header()] = None) -> str:
    """Stands in for real authentication: the token is the user's name."""
    if authorization is None:
        raise HTTPException(401, "Not authenticated", headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
    return authorization.removeprefix("Bearer ")


@app.get("/products/{product_id}")
@cache(expire=600, vary_headers=(), tags=lambda product_id, **_: [f"product:{product_id}"])
async def product(product_id: int) -> Product:
    """Public data: one entry per product, whoever asks (`vary_headers=()`)."""
    found = shop.product(product_id)
    if found is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such product")  # errors are never cached
    return found


@app.put("/products/{product_id}")
async def update_product(product_id: int, update: Product) -> Product:
    shop.products[product_id] = update
    await FastAPICache.invalidate_tags(f"product:{product_id}")
    return update


@app.get("/me")
@cache(expire=30)
async def me(user: Annotated[str, Depends(current_user)]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Personal data: an entry per Authorization header, never shared."""
    return {"user": user}


@app.get("/me/recommendations")
async def recommendations(
    user: Annotated[str, Depends(current_user)],
    app_cache: Annotated[Cache, Depends(get_cache)],
) -> list[Product]:
    async def load() -> list[Product]:  # annotated: the entry comes back as products
        return shop.recommendations(user)

    return await app_cache.get_or_set(f"recommendations:{user}", load, expire=300)


@cache(expire=3600)
async def exchange_rate(currency: str) -> float:
    """A slow call to another service, made at most once an hour per currency."""
    return {"USD": 1.08, "GBP": 0.86}.get(currency, 1.0)


@app.get("/products/{product_id}/price")
async def price(product_id: int, currency: str = "EUR") -> dict[str, float]:
    found = shop.product(product_id)
    if found is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such product")
    return {"price": round(found.price * await exchange_rate(currency), 2)}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

The repository also has examples/redis, with Redis, signed entries, a sync endpoint run in the thread pool and an HTML page cached with PickleCoder.

docs.title: Idempotency keys
docs.text: A payments API where a client that retries after a timeout or a dropped connection gets the first response again, instead of charging the card twice. IdempotencyMiddleware keeps each response under the client's Idempotency-Key, and require_idempotency_key makes POST /payments refuse requests without one. The responses are kept in the cache installed on the app, signed with its signing_key.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.idempotency.main:app

Stored responses are signed: set CACHE_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process, or a retry that reaches another process charges again. The example has two customers, alice and bob, whose tokens are alice-token and bob-token.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
A payment, with a new key:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/payments -H "Authorization: Bearer alice-token" \
    -H "Idempotency-Key: 8e03978e-40d5-43e8-bc93-6894a57f9324" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"amount": 1250, "currency": "EUR", "description": "Order 1042"}'
HTTP/1.1 201 Created

{"amount":1250,"currency":"EUR","description":"Order 1042","id":"ch_182671f5910f3ece","customer":"alice","created_at":"2026-10-26T10:57:18.321689Z"}

The same request again, as a client retries it, gets the same response without charging again:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/payments -H "Authorization: Bearer alice-token" \
    -H "Idempotency-Key: 8e03978e-40d5-43e8-bc93-6894a57f9324" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"amount": 1250, "currency": "EUR", "description": "Order 1042"}'
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
idempotent-replayed: true

{"amount":1250,"currency":"EUR","description":"Order 1042","id":"ch_182671f5910f3ece","customer":"alice","created_at":"2026-10-26T10:57:18.321689Z"}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/payments -H "Authorization: Bearer alice-token"
[{"amount":1250,"currency":"EUR","description":"Order 1042","id":"ch_182671f5910f3ece","customer":"alice","created_at":"2026-10-26T10:57:18.321689Z"}]

The same key with another body is a bug in the client, not a retry:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/payments -H "Authorization: Bearer alice-token" \
    -H "Idempotency-Key: 8e03978e-40d5-43e8-bc93-6894a57f9324" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"amount": 99000, "currency": "EUR", "description": "Order 1042"}'
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Content

{"detail": "This Idempotency-Key was used with a different request"}

Keys are per customer: Bob sending Alice's key gets a payment of his own, not hers:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/payments -H "Authorization: Bearer bob-token" \
    -H "Idempotency-Key: 8e03978e-40d5-43e8-bc93-6894a57f9324" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"amount": 1250, "currency": "EUR", "description": "Order 1042"}'
HTTP/1.1 201 Created

{"amount":1250,"currency":"EUR","description":"Order 1042","id":"ch_f9647245e9b65cf9","customer":"bob","created_at":"2026-10-26T10:57:19.339093Z"}

A payment without a key is refused:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/payments -H "Authorization: Bearer alice-token" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"amount": 1250, "currency": "EUR", "description": "Order 1042"}'
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request

{"detail":"This request needs an Idempotency-Key header"}

A retry that arrives while the first request is still charging the card (it takes a second) gets a 409 with Retry-After: 1 and {"detail": "A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed"}, and the card is charged once:

$ for attempt in first retry; do
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$attempt: %{http_code} after %{time_total}s\n" \
      -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/payments -H "Authorization: Bearer alice-token" \
      -H "Idempotency-Key: 5f0c1a8e-2b7d-4c39-9e61-0d4f8a3b7c25" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"amount": 4800, "currency": "EUR", "description": "Order 1043"}' &
    sleep 0.2
  done; wait
retry: 409 after 0.000958s
first: 201 after 1.002062s

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Keys per customer, not per token: identifier=customer_id makes the middleware look keys up among the requests of the same customer. The default, the Authorization header, suits API keys that never change; with access tokens that expire, a retry sent with a refreshed token would charge the card again.
  • The key is required where it matters: the middleware handles every POST and PATCH that carries an Idempotency-Key, and require_idempotency_key answers 400 to a payment without one. It runs after the authentication, so a request without a token gets a 401 first.
  • What's kept: the responses the endpoint gives, below 500. Not those refused before anything ran (a 401, a 422 for an invalid body): the client fixes the request and sends it with the same key. A retry must otherwise send the same body, byte for byte: it's what the 422 for "another request" compares.
  • Server errors run again: a 500 isn't kept, so a retry runs the payment again. That's why the key also goes to the provider (f"{customer}:{key}"): if the request fails after the charge, the provider's own idempotency keeps the card from being charged twice.
  • Signed responses: the cache's signing_key keeps whoever can write to Redis from planting a response for a retry. When the responses carry personal data, encryption_key encrypts them too.
  • Shared state: InMemoryBackend keeps the responses and locks in one process. With Redis or Valkey a retry finds the first response, and the 409, whichever process it reaches.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/idempotency/main.py
"""A payments API where a retried request never charges a card twice, thanks to idempotency keys.

    uvicorn examples.idempotency.main:app

Clients send a new `Idempotency-Key` (a random UUID) with each new payment, and the same key when
they retry it after a timeout or a dropped connection:

- A retry gets the first response again, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`: the card is charged
  once.
- A retry that arrives while the first request still runs gets a 409 with `Retry-After: 1`.
- The same key with another body gets a 422: that's a bug in the client, not a retry.
- Keys are per customer: nobody gets another customer's payment by sending their key.
- `POST /payments` without a key gets a 400.

The responses and the locks live in the cache's backend: InMemoryBackend here, so that it runs
without a server. Production uses Redis or Valkey, so that a retry finds the first response
whichever process it reaches.
"""

import asyncio
import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Annotated, Literal

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
from starlette.requests import HTTPConnection

from fastapi_alcazaba import Cache
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.idempotency import IdempotencyMiddleware, require_idempotency_key

# Stands in for your customers and their access tokens (a database, or a JWT check).
TOKENS = {"alice-token": "alice", "bob-token": "bob"}


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    # Signs the stored responses, so that whoever can write to Redis can't plant one for a
    # retry. Every process needs the same key, or a retry that reaches another process runs
    # again: set CACHE_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)). With personal data in the
    # responses, pass encryption_key= instead: they're encrypted too.
    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()


class NewPayment(BaseModel):
    amount: int = Field(gt=0, le=1_000_000, description="In cents")
    currency: Literal["EUR", "USD"]
    description: str = Field(default="", max_length=200)


class Payment(NewPayment):
    id: str
    customer: str
    created_at: datetime


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Production: RedisBackend(redis.asyncio.from_url(...)), with the URL in the settings, shared
    # by every process. Payments are a list in memory here, a table in your database.
    Cache(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="payments", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key).install(
        application
    )
    application.state.payments = []
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


def customer_id(connection: HTTPConnection) -> str:
    """Stands in for your authentication: the customer whose bearer token the request carries,
    "" if none."""
    scheme, _, token = connection.headers.get("authorization", "").partition(" ")
    return TOKENS.get(token, "") if scheme.lower() == "bearer" else ""


# Keys are looked up among the requests of the same customer. The default, the Authorization
# header, suits API keys that never change; with access tokens that expire, a retry sent with a
# refreshed token would charge the card again.
app.add_middleware(IdempotencyMiddleware, identifier=customer_id)


def current_customer(request: Request) -> str:
    if not (customer := customer_id(request)):
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
    return customer


def get_payments(request: Request) -> list[Payment]:
    payments: list[Payment] = request.app.state.payments
    return payments


Customer = Annotated[str, Depends(current_customer)]
# A 400 for requests without the header: a payment must never run without one.
IdempotencyKey = Annotated[str, Depends(require_idempotency_key)]
Payments = Annotated[list[Payment], Depends(get_payments)]


# pylint: disable-next=unused-argument  # a stand-in: the provider's client sends them all
async def charge_card(customer: str, payment: NewPayment, idempotency_key: str) -> str:
    """Stands in for the payment provider: charges the card, and returns the charge's id. The
    key goes to the provider too, which charges a key once however often it's asked."""
    await asyncio.sleep(1)  # the round trip to the card network
    return f"ch_{secrets.token_hex(8)}"


@app.post("/payments", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def pay(
    payment: NewPayment,
    customer: Customer,
    key: IdempotencyKey,
    payments: Payments,
) -> Payment:
    """Runs once per Idempotency-Key: retries get this response again."""
    # Server errors aren't kept, so a retry runs again. If this request fails after the charge,
    # the provider's own idempotency keys (Stripe's, Adyen's...) keep the card from being charged
    # twice: pass it this one, per customer like the middleware's.
    charge = await charge_card(customer, payment, idempotency_key=f"{customer}:{key}")
    receipt = Payment(
        id=charge, customer=customer, created_at=datetime.now(UTC), **payment.model_dump()
    )
    payments.append(receipt)
    return receipt


@app.get("/payments")
async def list_payments(customer: Customer, payments: Payments) -> list[Payment]:
    return [payment for payment in payments if payment.customer == customer]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: Rate and concurrency limits
docs.text: An API with a public search limited per client address, routes for signed-in users that share one budget per user (a report takes ten times as much of it as a list of orders), and a slow report endpoint that renders at most two reports at a time across every process. FastAPIRateLimiter counts the requests per minute, and FastAPIConcurrencyLimiter the ones in flight.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.limits.main:app

The example has three users, alice, bob and carol, whose tokens are alice-token, bob-token and carol-token.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
The public search allows 10 requests a minute per address. Every response says how many are left (r), and for how many seconds at least (t):

$ curl -i "http://127.0.0.1:8000/search?q=oli"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
ratelimit: "10/60s";r=9;t=16
ratelimit-policy: "10/60s";q=10;w=60

[{"name":"Olive oil","price":9.5},{"name":"Olives","price":3.2}]

The eleventh within the minute is refused, with the seconds to wait:

$ for i in $(seq 9); do curl -s -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:8000/search?q=oli"; done
$ curl -i "http://127.0.0.1:8000/search?q=oli"
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
ratelimit: "10/60s";r=0;t=22
ratelimit-policy: "10/60s";q=10;w=60
retry-after: 22

{"detail":"Too Many Requests"}

Signed-in users have one budget of 30 a minute for /orders and /reports together:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "Authorization: Bearer alice-token"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
ratelimit: "api";r=29;t=16
ratelimit-policy: "api";q=30;w=60

[{"id":1,"customer":"alice","total":12.5},{"id":2,"customer":"alice","total":25.0},{"id":3,"customer":"alice","total":37.5}]

A report takes 10 of it, and three seconds to render:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/reports -H "Authorization: Bearer alice-token" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"month": "2026-09"}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
ratelimit: "api";r=19;t=16
ratelimit-policy: "api";q=30;w=60

{"month":"2026-09","customer":"alice","pages":12}

After a second report Alice has 9 left: not enough for a third, but enough to list her orders. Bob's budget is his own:

$ curl -si -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/reports -H "Authorization: Bearer alice-token" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"month": "2026-10"}' | grep ratelimit:
ratelimit: "api";r=9;t=13

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/reports -H "Authorization: Bearer alice-token" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"month": "2026-08"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
ratelimit: "api";r=9;t=10
ratelimit-policy: "api";q=30;w=60
retry-after: 13

{"detail":"Too Many Requests"}

$ curl -si http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "Authorization: Bearer alice-token" | grep ratelimit:
ratelimit: "api";r=8;t=10

$ curl -si http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "Authorization: Bearer bob-token" | grep ratelimit:
ratelimit: "api";r=29;t=10

Without a valid token, a request is refused before it reaches any limiter:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Unauthorized"}

Three reports at once: two render, and the third waits 2 seconds for a slot, then gets a 503 with Retry-After: 3:

$ for month in 2026-07 2026-08 2026-09; do
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$month: %{http_code} after %{time_total}s\n" \
      -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/reports -H "Authorization: Bearer carol-token" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"month\": \"$month\"}" &
  done; wait
2026-08: 503 after 2.009854s
2026-09: 200 after 3.009745s
2026-07: 200 after 3.009700s

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Who a client is: /search counts by the address that the ASGI server reports (IPv6 addresses by their /64 network), never by X-Forwarded-For. uvicorn takes the address from that header only on connections from --forwarded-allow-ips (127.0.0.1 and ::1 by default, which is why a curl on the same machine can set it): set it to your proxy's address.
  • Authentication first: authenticate is a dependency of the router, so it runs before the routes' own dependencies. The limiter's identifier reads the user it found, and a request without a valid token gets its 401 before it takes anybody's budget.
  • One budget, several routes: the limiters made with api_budget have the same name and rate, so they share each user's 30 a minute; cost=10 makes a report take ten of them, and a user with 9 left can still list orders. Requests that fail validation count too: FastAPI runs the dependencies before it answers 422.
  • The budget before the slots: on /reports the rate limiter comes first, so a client over its budget is refused at once instead of waiting for a slot.
  • Slots for the slow part: the slot is held while the report renders and given back after the response is sent. name="reports" lets a job outside requests take the same slots with async with report_slots.slot().
  • Shared state: InMemoryBackend counts in one process. With Redis or Valkey every process shares the counters and slots; otherwise each one would allow 10 searches a minute and 2 reports at a time of its own.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/limits/main.py
"""An API with rate limits per client and per user, and a concurrency limit on its slowest
endpoint.

    uvicorn examples.limits.main:app

- `GET /search` is public: 10 requests a minute per client address (IPv6 addresses by their /64
  network, what an ISP gives a single customer).
- `GET /orders` and `POST /reports` are for signed-in users, and share one budget of 30 requests a
  minute per user, of which each report takes 10.
- `POST /reports` renders at most 2 reports at a time, across every process: a request waits up
  to 2 seconds for a slot, then gets a 503.

Over a rate limit, clients get a 429. Refused requests say when to retry (`Retry-After`), and
the other responses how much is left (`RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy`), for clients to slow
down before they get a 429.

The counters and the slots live in the cache's backend: InMemoryBackend here, so that it runs
without a server. Production uses Redis or Valkey, so that every process shares them.
"""

import asyncio
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from functools import partial
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Query, Request, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from starlette.requests import HTTPConnection

from fastapi_alcazaba import Cache, FastAPIConcurrencyLimiter, FastAPIRateLimiter
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend

# Stands in for your users and their access tokens (a database, or a JWT check).
TOKENS = {"alice-token": "alice", "bob-token": "bob", "carol-token": "carol"}


class Product(BaseModel):
    name: str
    price: float


class Order(BaseModel):
    id: int
    customer: str
    total: float


class ReportRequest(BaseModel):
    month: str = Field(pattern=r"^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$", examples=["2026-09"])


class Report(ReportRequest):
    customer: str
    pages: int


CATALOG = [
    Product(name="Olive oil", price=9.5),
    Product(name="Olives", price=3.2),
    Product(name="Oregano", price=2.1),
    Product(name="Orange jam", price=4.8),
]


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # InMemoryBackend counts in this process only. Production uses Redis or Valkey
    # (RedisBackend(redis.asyncio.from_url(...)), with the URL in the app's settings): with
    # several processes, each would otherwise allow its own 10 searches a minute and its own 2
    # reports at a time.
    Cache(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="limits").install(application)
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


@app.get("/search", dependencies=[Depends(FastAPIRateLimiter(10, minutes=1))])
async def search(q: Annotated[str, Query(min_length=2, max_length=50)]) -> list[Product]:
    """Public: 10 requests a minute per client address. Behind a proxy, let uvicorn take the
    address from its headers (`--proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips=<proxy address>`): the
    limiter never reads `X-Forwarded-For`, which any client can set."""
    return [product for product in CATALOG if q.lower() in product.name.lower()]


def authenticate(request: Request) -> str:
    """Stands in for your authentication: the user whose bearer token it is, else a 401."""
    scheme, _, token = request.headers.get("authorization", "").partition(" ")
    user = TOKENS.get(token) if scheme.lower() == "bearer" else None
    if user is None:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
    request.state.user_id = user
    return user


def user_id(connection: HTTPConnection) -> str:
    """Whose budget a request takes: the user that authenticate() found."""
    user: str = connection.state.user_id
    return user


User = Annotated[str, Depends(authenticate)]

# The router's dependencies run before the routes' own: user_id() finds the user, and requests
# without a valid token are refused before they take anybody's budget.
api = APIRouter(dependencies=[Depends(authenticate)])

# Limiters with the same name and rate share one budget, whatever the route; `cost=` makes a
# route take more of it.
api_budget = partial(FastAPIRateLimiter, 30, minutes=1, name="api", identifier=user_id)

# At most 2 reports at a time, whoever asks for them: each one keeps a CPU busy for seconds.
# Named, so that a job outside requests can take the same slots: `async with report_slots.slot()`.
report_slots = FastAPIConcurrencyLimiter(2, name="reports", wait=2, retry_after=3)


@api.get("/orders", dependencies=[Depends(api_budget())])
async def orders(user: User) -> list[Order]:
    return [Order(id=n, customer=user, total=12.5 * n) for n in range(1, 4)]


async def render_report(user: str, month: str) -> Report:
    """Stands in for the slow part: rendering a PDF, OCR, a call to an AI model."""
    await asyncio.sleep(3)
    return Report(customer=user, month=month, pages=12)


# The budget before the slots: a client over its budget is refused at once, instead of waiting
# for a slot first.
@api.post("/reports", dependencies=[Depends(api_budget(cost=10)), Depends(report_slots)])
async def create_report(report: ReportRequest, user: User) -> Report:
    """10 of the user's 30 a minute, and one of the 2 slots while it renders."""
    return await render_report(user, report.month)


app.include_router(api)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: Errors and observability
docs.text:
An orders API that is easy to operate. Its errors are RFC 9457 problem details, from FastAPIProblemDetails: a validation error says where and what without echoing what was sent, running out of stock is a Problem with an available member, and a bug is a bare 500 that tells the client nothing about it. RequestIDMiddleware gives every request an ID, which RequestIDLogFilter puts in every log line, uvicorn's included, and which comes back in a header and in every problem.

RequestTimeoutMiddleware gives every request a deadline: the slow sales report gets a 504 and its database connection back, while the CSV export streams for as long as it takes. health_router adds the probes of the load balancer, with the database as a critical check and the cache as a non-critical one. OpenTelemetry needs no code: under its zero-code instrumentation, Alcazaba's metrics and spans go out with the app's (Metrics and traces).

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
python examples/observability/main.py

That starts uvicorn with the example's LOGGING configuration, so that every log line carries the request's ID. uvicorn examples.observability.main:app serves the same app with uvicorn's default logging, without the IDs; to use the configuration with the uvicorn command, save it as JSON and pass --log-config.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
An order placed. The response has an X-Request-ID, and so does every line logged for it:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"product_id": 1, "quantity": 2}'
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: efdd515c85e68aefadfe379f34142eef

{"product_id":1,"quantity":2,"id":31}

2026-10-26 12:34:23,679 INFO [efdd515c85e68aefadfe379f34142eef] orders: Order 31 placed
2026-10-26 12:34:23,680 INFO [efdd515c85e68aefadfe379f34142eef] "POST /orders HTTP/1.1" 201 Created

A validation error says which field is wrong and why, but not what was sent: FastAPI's own answer would echo the input, passwords included.

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"product_id": 1, "quantity": "lots"}'
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Content
x-request-id: f25fd411982ef2db845915fd6c6591b6
content-type: application/problem+json

{"type":"about:blank","title":"Unprocessable Content","status":422,"instance":"/orders","errors":[{"loc":["body","quantity"],"msg":"Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer","type":"int_parsing"}],"request_id":"f25fd411982ef2db845915fd6c6591b6"}

Running out of stock is a problem of the API's own, with its type and an available member that a client can act on:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"product_id": 2, "quantity": 5}'
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
x-request-id: 3905c40b8fa0c37707adf6b910773f47
content-type: application/problem+json

{"type":"https://example.com/problems/out-of-stock","title":"Out of stock","status":409,"detail":"Only 3 left","instance":"/orders","available":3,"request_id":"3905c40b8fa0c37707adf6b910773f47"}

A bug: the invoice's PDF renderer refuses the connection, and nothing handles it. The client gets a bare 500 with nothing about the renderer, and the request ID to quote. Here the client sent the ID itself, as a proxy would, and it was kept:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/3/invoice -H "X-Request-ID: support-ticket-4512"
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
x-request-id: support-ticket-4512
content-type: application/problem+json

{"type":"about:blank","title":"Internal Server Error","status":500,"instance":"/orders/3/invoice","request_id":"support-ticket-4512"}

The server logs the traceback under that ID:

2026-10-26 12:34:23,692 INFO [support-ticket-4512] "GET /orders/3/invoice HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
2026-10-26 12:34:23,692 ERROR [support-ticket-4512] uvicorn.error: Exception in ASGI application
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../examples/observability/main.py", line 140, in invoice
    raise ConnectionError(f"pdf-renderer.internal:9000 refused the invoice of order {order_id}")
ConnectionError: pdf-renderer.internal:9000 refused the invoice of order 3

The sales report takes 30 s. At the 10 s deadline the query is cancelled, its connection goes back to the pool and the client gets a 504. The middleware answers it itself, and with FastAPIProblemDetails installed its answer is a problem too:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/reports/sales
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
x-request-id: 7ec602139e1478ad0c023637123c599e
content-type: application/problem+json

{"type":"about:blank","title":"Gateway Timeout","status":504,"detail":"Request timed out","instance":"/reports/sales","request_id":"7ec602139e1478ad0c023637123c599e"}

2026-10-26 15:22:34,756 WARNING [7ec602139e1478ad0c023637123c599e] fastapi_alcazaba.observability.timeouts: GET /reports/sales timed out after 10.0s: answered 504

The export has no deadline: its 30 rows stream for 15 s, and it isn't cut short.

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{content_type} %{size_download} bytes in %{time_total}s\n' \
    http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/export
200 text/csv; charset=utf-8 231 bytes in 15.539356s

The probes. Readiness runs the checks and says how each went; liveness only says that the process answers:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/ready
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
cache-control: no-store
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: 577fa3fd67c00a6bd4b80cbf29256384

{"status":"ok","checks":{"database":{"status":"ok","duration_ms":0.014},"cache":{"status":"ok","duration_ms":0.012}}}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/live
{"status":"ok"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The order of the middlewares: the last one added is the outermost. RequestIDMiddleware goes around the deadline, so that the 504 has an ID too. A 500 is answered outside every middleware, by Starlette, and FastAPIProblemDetails adds the ID to it itself.
  • The filter on the handlers: a logger's filters don't see the records of its children, so RequestIDLogFilter goes on both handlers of the logging configuration, and uvicorn's access and error lines get the ID along with the app's.
  • Nothing to learn from an error: validation errors never carry the input, the 500 says nothing about the renderer, and the database's db.internal:5432: connection refused would be logged by the readiness check, never returned to a public probe.
  • A deadline gives resources back: the connection is a yield dependency, so it goes back to the pool when the deadline cancels the request. The export is exempt (paths={"/orders/export": None}): once a response has started it can't become a 504, it would only be cut short.
  • Critical or not: a failing database makes /health/ready a 503 and takes the process out of the load balancer; a failing cache only makes it degraded, since the cache fails open and taking every process out would turn its outage into a full one.
  • OpenTelemetry without code: run the app under opentelemetry-instrument. The FastAPI instrumentation traces each request, and Alcazaba's metrics (fastapi_alcazaba.problems, .request_timeouts, .request_ids, .health.checks…) go out through the same SDK.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/observability/main.py
"""An orders API that is easy to operate: errors, request IDs, deadlines and health checks.

    python examples/observability/main.py  # uvicorn, with the logging configuration below

- Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`): a validation error says where
  and what, never the values sent; running out of stock is a `Problem` with an `available`
  member; a bug is a bare 500 that tells the client nothing about it.
- Every request has an ID, in the `X-Request-ID` response header, in every problem and in every
  log line, uvicorn's included: a client quotes it, and its lines are found in the logs.
- Every request has a deadline: the slow sales report gets a 504 and its database connection
  back, while the CSV export streams for as long as it takes.
- `/health/live` and `/health/ready` for the load balancer: the database is a critical check, the
  cache a non-critical one.

OpenTelemetry needs nothing here. Run the app under its zero-code instrumentation
(`opentelemetry-instrument`, see "Metrics and traces" in the guide): the FastAPI instrumentation
traces each request, and Alcazaba's metrics (problems, request_timeouts, request_ids,
health.checks...) go out through the meter of the app's cache.
"""

import asyncio
import logging
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Any

import uvicorn
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, status
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from fastapi_alcazaba import Cache, FastAPIProblemDetails, Problem
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.observability import (
    RequestIDMiddleware,
    RequestTimeoutMiddleware,
    health_router,
)

logger = logging.getLogger("orders")

LOG_FORMAT = "%(asctime)s %(levelname)s [%(request_id)s] %(name)s: %(message)s"
ACCESS_FORMAT = '%(asctime)s %(levelname)s [%(request_id)s] "%(request_line)s" %(status_code)s'
# uvicorn's log_config. The filter goes on every handler (a logger's filters don't see the records
# of its children), so uvicorn's access and error lines carry the ID too. Plain JSON: for the
# uvicorn command, save it to a file and pass --log-config.
LOGGING: dict[str, Any] = {
    "version": 1,
    "disable_existing_loggers": False,
    "filters": {"request_id": {"()": "fastapi_alcazaba.observability.RequestIDLogFilter"}},
    "formatters": {
        "default": {"format": LOG_FORMAT},
        "access": {"()": "uvicorn.logging.AccessFormatter", "fmt": ACCESS_FORMAT},
    },
    "handlers": {
        name: {"class": "logging.StreamHandler", "formatter": name, "filters": ["request_id"]}
        for name in ("default", "access")
    },
    "loggers": {"uvicorn.access": {"handlers": ["access"], "level": "INFO", "propagate": False}},
    "root": {"handlers": ["default"], "level": "INFO"},
}


class NewOrder(BaseModel):
    product_id: int = Field(gt=0)
    quantity: int = Field(gt=0, le=100)


class Order(NewOrder):
    id: int


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database and its connection pool."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.stock = {1: 25, 2: 3}  # units left, by product
        self.orders = [Order(id=n, product_id=1, quantity=1) for n in range(1, 31)]
        self.in_use = 0  # connections taken from the pool
        self.up = True
        self.report_seconds = 30.0  # the sales report is a slow query
        self.row_seconds = 0.5  # and the export reads its rows slowly

    async def ping(self) -> None:
        if not self.up:
            # What drivers say: a host and a port that a public probe mustn't show anyone.
            raise ConnectionRefusedError("db.internal:5432: connection refused")


async def connection(request: Request) -> AsyncIterator[Database]:
    """A connection from the pool, given back when the request ends, also when it times out."""
    db: Database = request.app.state.db
    db.in_use += 1
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.in_use -= 1


DB = Annotated[Database, Depends(connection)]
router = APIRouter()


@router.post("/orders", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def place_order(new: NewOrder, db: DB) -> Order:
    if new.product_id not in db.stock:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, "No such product")  # a 4xx's detail is sent
    available = db.stock[new.product_id]
    if new.quantity > available:
        raise Problem(
            status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT,
            f"Only {available} left",
            type="https://example.com/problems/out-of-stock",
            title="Out of stock",
            extensions={"available": available},
        )
    db.stock[new.product_id] -= new.quantity
    order = Order(id=len(db.orders) + 1, **new.model_dump())
    db.orders.append(order)
    logger.info("Order %d placed", order.id)  # the filter adds the request's ID
    return order


@router.get("/orders/export")
async def export_orders(db: DB) -> StreamingResponse:
    """Every order as CSV, sent as the rows are read. It has no deadline (see `paths` below): once
    a response has started it can't become a 504, it would only be cut short."""

    async def rows() -> AsyncIterator[str]:
        yield "id,product_id,quantity\n"
        for order in list(db.orders):
            await asyncio.sleep(db.row_seconds)
            yield f"{order.id},{order.product_id},{order.quantity}\n"

    return StreamingResponse(rows(), media_type="text/csv")


@router.get("/orders/{order_id}/invoice")
async def invoice(order_id: int) -> dict[str, str]:
    """A failure nobody handled: the client gets a bare 500 with the request ID to quote, and the
    server logs the traceback under that ID."""
    raise ConnectionError(f"pdf-renderer.internal:9000 refused the invoice of order {order_id}")


@router.get("/reports/sales")
async def sales_report(db: DB) -> dict[str, int]:
    """At the deadline the query is cancelled, the connection goes back to the pool and the
    client gets a 504, instead of both waiting for as long as the query takes."""
    await asyncio.sleep(db.report_seconds)
    return {"orders": len(db.orders)}


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    application.state.db = Database()
    yield


def create_app(*, request_timeout: float = 10.0) -> FastAPI:
    """The application, with a deadline of `request_timeout` seconds per request."""
    application = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
    # In memory: nothing but this process reads or writes it. Alcazaba's metrics are recorded
    # through it, and /health/ready checks it.
    Cache(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="orders").install(application)
    FastAPIProblemDetails().install(application)
    application.include_router(router)

    async def database() -> None:
        await application.state.db.ping()

    application.include_router(health_router({"database": database}))
    # The last middleware added is the outermost. RequestIDMiddleware goes around the deadline, so
    # that the 504 it answers carries the ID too. (A 500 is answered outside every middleware;
    # FastAPIProblemDetails adds the ID to it itself.)
    application.add_middleware(
        RequestTimeoutMiddleware, timeout=request_timeout, paths={"/orders/export": None}
    )
    # Keeps a safe X-Request-ID set by the proxy (or the client); trust_incoming=False if clients
    # reach the application directly and shouldn't choose their IDs.
    application.add_middleware(RequestIDMiddleware)
    return application


app = create_app()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True, log_config=LOGGING)

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
An app operated at runtime, without a deploy, through a small admin API that takes a bearer token. It closes and reopens the app with FastAPIMaintenance, whose middleware answers 503 with Retry-After to everything but the health check and the admin routes. It defines FastAPIFeatureFlags: a new checkout rolled out to a percentage of the users, and a beta page that only the users on an allow list can see (a 404 for everybody else). And a FastAPIBreaker turns the failures of a flaky shipping service into a fast 503 while it's down.

The maintenance switch and the flags live in the backend, so a change made through one process reaches all of them. Each process keeps a copy for up to 1 s (maintenance) or 5 s (flags), so that requests don't each ask the backend. The breaker is each process's own.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.operations.main:app

The admin routes take Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN. Set ADMIN_TOKEN and CACHE_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process. Without ADMIN_TOKEN, the app makes one up at each start and logs it:

ADMIN_TOKEN isn't set: the admin token of this run is YbLt_8-WKnm4zWknL3mgHNar4E3MmBsCNtk6KPJLBB4

It keeps the switch and the flags in memory, so don't start it with --workers: each worker would have a switch of its own. In production, a Redis or Valkey backend lets every process share them.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
$ TOKEN=YbLt_8-WKnm4zWknL3mgHNar4E3MmBsCNtk6KPJLBB4

Without the token, the admin routes answer 401:

$ curl -i -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/maintenance -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}'
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Unauthorized"}

Close the app for maintenance. Every request gets a 503 with the message and Retry-After, but the health check is still served:

$ curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/maintenance -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"message": "Back at 10:30", "retry_after": 900}'
{"enabled":true,"message":"Back at 10:30","retry_after":900,"since":1793011967.4372241}

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/checkout
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
cache-control: no-store
retry-after: 900

{"detail": "Back at 10:30"}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
{"status":"ok"}

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/maintenance -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/checkout
{"checkout":"classic"}

Roll the new checkout out to 30 % of the users. Here the bearer token stands for the user, so that you can try it with curl. Each user keeps their answer from one request to the next, and anonymous visitors aren't part of a partial rollout:

$ curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/flags/new-checkout -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"enabled": true, "percentage": 30}'
{"name":"new-checkout","enabled":true,"percentage":30.0,"allow":[],"deny":[]}

$ for user in ana bea carlos david elena; do
>   echo "$user: $(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/checkout -H "Authorization: Bearer $user")"
> done
ana: {"checkout":"new"}
bea: {"checkout":"classic"}
carlos: {"checkout":"classic"}
david: {"checkout":"new"}
elena: {"checkout":"classic"}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/checkout
{"checkout":"classic"}

The beta report is a 404, like a page that doesn't exist, until the user is on the allow list. Without a percentage, a flag with an allow list is for nobody else. The list comes back as digests: the backend never gets the users' ids.

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/reports/beta -H "Authorization: Bearer ana"
{"detail":"Not Found"}

$ curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/flags/beta-reports -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"enabled": true, "allow": ["ana"]}'
{"name":"beta-reports","enabled":true,"percentage":null,"allow":["44d27c2ae32d479abf13f231ea9ee8295988d4a14fdf8be30c16aa81e894946b"],"deny":[]}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/reports/beta -H "Authorization: Bearer ana"
{"report":"Sales by hour"}

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/reports/beta -H "Authorization: Bearer bea"
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found

{"detail":"Not Found"}

Make the shipping service fail. The first three requests wait for it and get a 502; then the breaker opens, and requests get a 503 at once, without calling the service:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/7/shipping
{"order_id":7,"carrier":"Alhambra Express","days":2}

$ curl -X PUT "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/simulate/shipping?down=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/7/shipping    # three times
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway

{"detail":"The shipping service failed"}

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/7/shipping
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
retry-after: 30

{"detail":"Service Unavailable"}

The status page reads the shared state from the backend, and the breaker from this process:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/status -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
{"maintenance":{"enabled":false,"message":null,"retry_after":null,"since":null},"flags":{"new-checkout":{...},"beta-reports":{...}},"process":{"pid":831700,"shipping_breaker":"open"}}

The breaker stays open for 30 s, even when the service is back. Then a single request tries it, and its success closes the breaker:

$ curl -X PUT "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/simulate/shipping?down=false" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/7/shipping
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
retry-after: 30

{"detail":"Service Unavailable"}

$ sleep 30; curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/7/shipping
{"order_id":7,"carrier":"Alhambra Express","days":2}

Or, once you know the service is back, close the breaker at once. Only in the process that gets the request: each process has its own.

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/breakers/shipping/close -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/7/shipping
{"order_id":7,"carrier":"Alhambra Express","days":2}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The admin token is compared in constant time, as bytes: secrets.compare_digest takes the same time however much of a guess is right. It compares bytes because on strings it raises when a client sends non-ASCII characters: a 500 instead of a 401.
  • Shared state, local copies: the switch and the flags are in the backend, signed with CACHE_SIGNING_KEY, so a state planted there by someone else is ignored. Each process reads them again at most every refresh seconds, so a change takes up to 1 s (maintenance) or 5 s (flags) to reach the other processes; the process that made it, and /admin/status, see it at once. The breaker is created in the lifespan, one per process: it opens after that process's failures, with no round trip on every call.
  • /health and /admin are always served: the orchestrator doesn't restart processes that are only in maintenance, and the API that closed the app can reopen it.
  • Flag names are an enum: no flag the app never reads can be created. A flag with an allow list and no percentage is only for the list, so a beta never goes to everyone by mistake.
  • Subjects come from authentication: a route hidden by flags.require() takes its subject from a function of the request. Here the bearer token is the user id; in a real app take it from a session or a token you verify, or anyone could put themselves on an allow list.
  • Only what says the service is down opens the breaker: failures=(ConnectionError,), so a bug of ours doesn't, and a call that hangs is cancelled after 5 s and counts too. A failure is a 502; a refusal while the breaker is open, a 503 with Retry-After.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/operations/main.py
"""Operating an app without a deploy: maintenance mode, feature flags and a circuit breaker.

    uvicorn examples.operations.main:app

- `PUT /admin/maintenance` closes the app: a 503 with `Retry-After` for every request but
  `/health` (the load balancer keeps the processes) and `/admin` (you can reopen it).
- `PUT /admin/flags/{name}`: `new-checkout` goes to a percentage of the users, always the same
  ones; `/reports/beta` is a 404 but for the users on the allow list of `beta-reports`.
- `/orders/{order_id}/shipping` calls a flaky shipping service (simulated). After 3 failures in a
  row, each a 502 that waited for it, the breaker opens: a 503 at once for 30 s, without calling
  it. Then one request tries again; `POST /admin/breakers/shipping/close` closes it at once.

The admin routes take `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN`.

The maintenance switch and the flags live in the backend, shared by every process. Each process
keeps a copy, read again at most every 1 s (maintenance) or 5 s (flags): requests don't each ask
the backend, and a change reaches every process within that. Breakers are each process's own:
one opens after its process's failures, with no round trip on every call.
"""

import logging
import os
import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Annotated, Any

import uvicorn
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, status
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
from starlette.requests import HTTPConnection

from fastapi_alcazaba import (
    BackendUnavailable,
    FastAPIBreaker,
    FastAPICache,
    FastAPIFeatureFlags,
    FastAPIMaintenance,
)
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.operations import MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH, FeatureFlag, MaintenanceMiddleware
from fastapi_alcazaba.operations.maintenance import MaintenanceStatus

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file. Set both in production, the
    same in every process (secrets.token_urlsafe(32))."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    admin_token: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    # Seals the switch and the flags in the backend: a state planted there by someone else is
    # ignored, and so is what a process with another key writes.
    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()


class Flag(StrEnum):
    """The flags this app reads: the admin routes define only these."""

    NEW_CHECKOUT = "new-checkout"
    BETA_REPORTS = "beta-reports"


class Quote(BaseModel):
    order_id: int
    carrier: str
    days: int


class ShippingService:
    """Stands in for a downstream service and its SDK: fails while `down`, and counts the calls
    that reach it."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.down = False
        self.calls = 0

    async def quote(self, order_id: int) -> Quote:
        self.calls += 1
        if self.down:
